title: Prescriptive rewrite: every chapter re-read under ADR-0032, ratchet to zero
description:
Umbrella for the review ADR-0032 started. The set became prescriptive and implementation-agnostic on 2026-09-12 (spec-repo PR #1, merge c6354f3); the rules landed there and each chapter is now re-read under them, one pull request per chapter, in dependency order.

READ FIRST, every ticket: docs/adr/0032-specification-is-prescriptive-and-implementation-agnostic.md (the decision, the refactor test, the fate of each chapter), README.md 'Requirement conventions' and 'How compliance is measured', AGENTS.md.

The refactor test: a sentence is a requirement only if a rewrite that keeps every byte on disk, every byte on the wire and every observable behaviour identical CANNOT violate it. On-disk shapes, wire shapes, protocol facts and persisted/serialized type names stay. Function and method names, crate and file paths, line numbers, frameworks, the fork pin, the actor mechanism go; their behaviours and invariants stay as requirements.

Done-condition shared by every chapter ticket:
1. Every requirement in the chapter re-read, not re-moded: states a behaviour observable at a boundary (federation/gateway, seed, frontend, durability); says what the wallet SHOULD do, so where today's code differs the requirement changes and the code gains a finding; buildable from the text alone.
2. Requirements that described only a codebase fact are withdrawn: id removed, row added to README.md 'Withdrawn identifiers' (Identifier | Was | Why it went). Never renumber, never reuse.
3. New behaviour a re-read exposes gets the next free id in its namespace.
4. tools/codebase-refs-baseline.txt: the chapter's line lowered to its new count (target 0) in the same PR.
5. bash tools/check-all.sh exit 0, run unpiped, before and after.
6. The PR description carries a HAND-OFF LIST for the code repository: each Fn in douglaz/fedimint-wallets/docs/open-findings.md whose sense changes (gap-vs-decision becomes non-conformance-vs-requirement), each new non-conformance a strengthened requirement creates, and each finding a withdrawn requirement orphans. A code-repo bead is cut from that list when the PR merges; it is not this ticket's work.
7. One PR per chapter; the two review bots (Codex connector, CodeRabbit) run on every push; address findings, then merge.

Order (blocking edges): 00 → 01 → 02 → 03 → 05 → 06 → 04 → 07 → 08 → 09 → 10 → final pass. Persistence before allocator because ALC cites STO properties; API after the lifecycle because 04 is the wire view of 03.

title: Chapter 02 fedimint integration: rewrite under ADR-0032 (fork pin out, patched behaviours in)
description:
Rewrite 02-fedimint-integration.md prescriptively. Baseline today: 35 lines — second heaviest. This chapter is where 'environment vs codebase' bites: the Fedimint federation and gateway protocols are presupposed and cited freely; the SDK's internal API is not.
Decided in ADR-0032:
- FMI-1 (the douglaz/fedimint fork pin at a revision) and FMI-2 (any repoint carries every patch) GO. Each behaviour the three patches provide becomes its own FMI requirement: iroh long-poll bound, recovery complete-or-fail, single-share TPE correctness. Hand-off: F19 (the pin) becomes 'satisfied by fork patch, not upstream' compliance notes on those requirements; F20 (lnv2 claim-retry / reclaim_receive) is a non-conformance against a new requirement that a Stranded move has a recovery path — write that requirement.
- FMI-7 seed derivation STAYS and becomes normative with the derivation stated, no SDK names: two implementations must derive the same keys or recovery is not implementation-independent.
- FMI-11 keeps the routing_info exchange (protocol) and loses 'pooled HTTP client'; F45 (SSRF egress) is a non-conformance against a new SEC/FMI requirement restricting egress — coordinate with the 07 ticket, decide the owner here and cite from 07.
- FMI-13 gateway_serves_route(to, from, gw), FMI-36 MultiClient::new/ConnectorRegistry, FMI-3 'four modules on one ClientBuilder' — restate as behaviour (which modules a joined federation must expose; how transport is decided by invite and config).
- FMI-10 'the SDK's list_gateways(None)' — the vetted list is defined by ADR-0029 (threshold-vetted, read per guardian); write the requirement to the ADR, F6 becomes the non-conformance.
- FMI-19 'enforced at the pin, on the wrong ordering' — descriptive of a defect; the requirement is the correct ordering (component-wise), the current behaviour is a finding.
Hand-off: F6, F19, F20, F45 change sense; possibly new findings for FMI-19.
See the epic for the shared done-condition.

title: Chapter 03 operation lifecycle: rewrite under ADR-0032 (invariants stay, actor goes)
description:
Rewrite 03-operation-lifecycle.md prescriptively. Baseline today: 22 lines. The chapter's substance — admission, execution, resumption, terminalization, the four killpoints, supersession, reconcile — is behaviour and stays. What goes is the mechanism: 'through the actor', 'Runtime::tick', 'Runtime::do_move', 'the standalone path bypasses the actor' (OPS-12, OPS-5 etc). Per ADR-0032 the invariants are requirements: one serialized admission point; one live key per allocator goal; agent work admitted nowhere else; generation-fenced writes; no operation's network IO on the admission point. State them as MUSTs on the wallet, not on an actor.
The standalone tick admission exception (ADR-0031, CONTEXT.md Engine) is behaviour and stays.
OPS-39 (RefuseReason by message substring) is a wire contract nobody documented as one — under the prescriptive posture decide: either the reason codes are the contract (write the table as normative, message text informative) or the substrings are; recommend codes. Hand-off: F37 changes sense.
F42 (standalone probe bypasses actor) and F44 (user move attaches to a probe leg) are non-conformances against the admission invariants once written; F8 (refused-after-commit row on the planned pair) against the ledger-correctness requirement — say which requirement each violates in the hand-off.
See the epic for the shared done-condition.

title: Chapter 05 persistence: rewrite under ADR-0032 (on-disk shapes stay, write paths go)
description:
Rewrite 05-persistence.md prescriptively. Baseline today: 43 lines — the heaviest chapter, and the one where the refactor test does the most work. ON DISK STAYS: two stores (STO-1), the advisory lock file (STO-2), partition prefixes (STO-3), the seed encoding (STO-4), key tags and value encodings (STO-5), correlation/idempotency key shapes (STO-6), every persisted row field by field (STO-9..15, 26), the serde-rules-as-encoding (STO-29..31: a field added to a persisted type MUST decode when absent; no persisted type rejects unknown fields). These are an upgrade-in-place contract.
GOES: 'enforced by the pure advance function' (STO-16), 'repair_ledger scans' (STO-24), wallet_core::MoveRecord paths, 'fedimint's raw byte transactions' as mechanism (STO-7 — keep the atomicity property), which writer performs a write. Keep every PROPERTY: write discipline, CAS fencing (STO-8), O(1) sequence assignment (STO-18), one current row per correlation key (STO-20), the Agent occurrence floor (STO-21..23), unreadable rows never fence automation (STO-22), terminal immutability, the OPS-24 ordering.
STO-32 ('greenfield in one respect... unverified against the long-running deployment's store') is deployment content: the requirement is that the two fields decode when absent like every other; F38 is the check against one store and stays a code-repo item. STO-19 'full ascending scan, reverses' is an algorithm — keep the observable (history is newest-first, paged by before_seq), drop the scan.
Hand-off: F12 (no app-state backup) — decide whether a snapshot/restore is a requirement (ADR-0025 says the seed is the backup unit; Restore is an operator action) or stays a code-repo task; F38, F41 sense; F7 (committed route not persisted) is a non-conformance against the Committed route requirement (cite ADR-0030).
See the epic for the shared done-condition.

title: Chapter 06 allocator and automation: rewrite under ADR-0032
description:
Rewrite 06-allocator-and-automation.md prescriptively. Baseline today: 22 lines. The decision core is already stated as a pure function over a snapshot — keep that as a requirement (determinism, no IO) without naming decide(). Route economics, scoring, probes, discovery, evacuation, the tick, the scheduler cycle and the readiness signal are behaviour.
Watch for: ALC-15 'unreachable in production' (the scorer's activity buckets) — a prescriptive set does not carry dead branches; either the buckets are required behaviour with a stated input, or the requirement is withdrawn. ALC-19 (two evacuation leads with one name) — decide the requirement: one lead, or two with distinct names; F36 becomes the non-conformance. ALC-45..49 (readiness, the fourth invisible suppression, eight fail-closed paths without a ledger row, the light probe four times per cycle) are currently written as descriptions of defects: rewrite each as the requirement (every suppression reported on /v1/health; every fail-closed path leaves a row; the light probe runs once per cycle or the count is a stated requirement) and hand off F32, F33, F34 as non-conformances. 'Runtime::watch_once is a dev/test harness with no production caller' fails the refactor test — withdraw or restate as 'no host schedules through anything but the engine's cycle'. ALC-50 (cfg(test) seams) is codebase — withdraw.
The F1 shortfall-with-no-signal: requirement = every withheld funding decision is recorded (see 00 ticket); F1 non-conformance. F10 (no aggregate ceiling) — decide whether an aggregate exposure cap is a requirement (recommend yes, since exposure otherwise scales with joins) and hand off. F15 (conflict-suppressed goals not in status) likewise.
Hand-off: F1, F10, F14, F15, F32, F33, F34, F36 change sense; F3 (hop unbuilt) is a non-conformance against ADR-0029's requirements — make sure the hop requirement is written here, not only in the ADR.

title: Chapter 07 security: rewrite under ADR-0032
description:
Rewrite 07-security-requirements.md prescriptively. Baseline today: 3 lines — light on codebase refs, heavy on 'what is actually enforced — including what is not', which is the descriptive posture in its purest form. Every 'not enforced' becomes either a requirement (and a finding in the hand-off) or a decided non-goal citing its ADR.
Known items:
- The seed at rest (SEC-n citing ADR-0026). Write the requirement at the level ADR-0026 DECIDED, no further: the seed MUST NOT be stored in plaintext; it is protected by AEAD over the stored entropy under a key not stored beside it; when the key source is unavailable at start the wallet fails closed and never falls back to plaintext; mnemonic export and restore-mnemonic keep working. The KEY SOURCE (operator passphrase with a memory-hard KDF vs KMS/HSM) is a RECOMMENDATION in ADR-0026 'to ratify in the implementation bead', not a decision — do not ratify it through this rewrite. If the 07 PR wants to settle it, propose an ADR-0026 amendment in the PR and let it be accepted on its own; until then the requirement is silent on key derivation. F11 is the non-conformance.
- SEC-17 (no ADR records the per-guardian response bound) — write the bound as a requirement or withdraw the sentence.
- SEC-20 / DEF-22 (deployment identity not in tracked files) is a code-repo hygiene rule about one tree, not a wallet requirement — withdraw SEC-20 here (DEF-22 handled by the 09 ticket).
- SEC-24 (an id alone carries no guardian endpoints) stays.
- F45 egress restriction: the owner is decided by the 02 ticket; cite it from here.
Threat model: keep, as the frame the requirements answer. Remove any 'today the code does X' hedges.
Hand-off: F11, F21 (deployment identity in git history — code-repo only, no spec requirement), F45 sense.

title: Chapter 09 known defects: keep the prohibitions, drop the provenance

title: Chapter 10 conformance: the normative scenario suite
description:
Rewrite 10-conformance-checklist.md as the normative scenario suite (ADR-0032). Baseline today: 11 lines. Each surviving CNF-n is a scenario — given / when / then — at the wallet's boundaries, names the requirements it demonstrates ('demonstrates: ALC-20, DEF-21'), and carries NO result: no checkbox, no commit hash, no test function name, no run date, no gate command line. Add the sentence that makes it normative: a conformant implementation MUST pass every scenario.
Scenarios are stated against the wallet's ENVIRONMENT — two federations, their gateways, a Lightning node, a crash at a named point — never against a harness. devimint is the reference implementation's harness and lives in the code repository; a scenario does not name it, any harness that produces the given state is admissible, and how the code repository realises each scenario is its conformance-results file's business.
WITHDRAW (README rows): process discipline CNF-1, CNF-2, CNF-3, CNF-30, CNF-39, CNF-40 (to the code repo's AGENTS.md — most already there); build/unit results CNF-4, CNF-5; work items wearing a CNF id: CNF-45 (human reading of four boundaries, F26), CNF-46 (sidecar, F27), CNF-47 (seed re-encryption, F11), CNF-48 (restore drill) — their Fn already track them. Every other unchecked box is either a scenario nobody has run (keep as a scenario; the code repo's results say unrun) or a finding (withdraw, hand off).
ADD scenarios the chapter rewrites exposed as missing: the flat-cap regression DEF-25 / F22 (an evacuation whose parameters discriminate the cap basis), the after-receive-commit killpoint F25, the recovery FAILURE path F24, delivered≠ask at the pre-mint gate F23. Each is a scenario here and a non-conformance ('scenario not yet runnable/passing') in the hand-off.
Verify: every requirement in 02–08 that claims to be demonstrable cites a CNF, and every CNF cites at least one requirement. Baseline to 0.
Hand-off: F22, F23, F24, F25, F26 sense; the checkbox state at c6354f3 as the code repo's initial conformance-results file.

title: OPS-20 follow-up: the planned-cap fallback for an Evacuate row without fee_cap is looser than the enforced cap
description:
Raised by CodeRabbit on spec-repo PR #7 (chapter 05) and deferred there because OPS-20 (03) owns
the precedence. OPS-20's cap precedence for reassembly is artifact > cached (only when the cache
holds a receive or send operation id) > planned. A committed receive operation whose MoveMeta
carries no `fee_cap` (a row an older build wrote; STO-33 says absent decodes as none, never zero)
therefore falls back to the intent's PLANNED cap. For an `Evacuate` the planned cap is
`fee_cap_components.at(planned amount)`, and the planned amount is larger than the delivered net,
so the reconstructed cap is LOOSER than the cap that was enforced at the sized net — the pairing
DEF-4 / STO-17 exists to prevent (an auditor recomputing the cap from an amount nobody received).

Decide, in 03: should the fallback for an `Evacuate` (an intent carrying `fee_cap_components`)
be `fee_cap_components.at(meta.amount)` — the leg's own `amount` IS on the metadata (STO-33),
so the enforced cap is reconstructible without the cache — with the planned cap only for an
action without components? Or state that such a row is not rebuildable and the pay step
re-checks under the planned cap (OPS-26 already re-quotes both legs against rec.fee_cap)?

Owner: OPS-20 (and OPS-26 if the re-check wording changes). Land as one clause; cite ADR-0029
("the cap enforced at that net") and CONTEXT.md **Delivered net**. Any code that falls back to
the planned cap today becomes a non-conformance in the code repo's open-findings.md.
Gate: bash tools/check-all.sh exit 0 before and after; 03's ratchet baseline stays 0.
close_reason: Landed in spec-repo PR #14 (e360604): OPS-20's cap fallback is the action's cap rule at the reassembled amount; OPS-25 cites it; code-repo bead br-ops20-capless-leg-fallback-nb8 tracks the implementation check

title: Four-model review 2026-09-23: blockers and majors
description:
Umbrella for the findings of the 2026-09-23 independent review of the whole set (Fable, Opus, gpt-6-astra, gpt-5.6-sol; same prompt, read-only, full corpus at cd4ea86). Consensus verdict: NOT BUILDABLE as written — an implementer with only this repository and the public Fedimint SDK cannot produce a wallet compliant with every MUST at once. Consolidated report with every citation: ~/spec-review/CONSOLIDATED.md (raw per-model reports beside it).

Shared done-condition for every child: (1) the contradiction or gap is resolved in the OWNING requirement, everywhere else cites the id (README, One owner per rule); (2) a decision nobody has taken goes to 11-open-questions.md and the set stays silent, per AGENTS.md; (3) a new rule gets the next free id in its namespace, withdrawn ids get a README row; (4) where the requirement can be demonstrated, 10-conformance-checklist.md gains or amends the scenario and the requirement cites it; (5) bash tools/check-all.sh exit 0, unpiped, before and after; (6) any requirement whose sense changes for the existing implementation is listed as a hand-off for the code repository's docs/open-findings.md.

Priority 0 children are the three blockers; priority 1 are the majors. Every finding marked verified was re-checked against the cited lines by the orchestrating session; plausible ones were not.

## Corrected after the 2026-09-23 four-model bead review (reports: ~/spec-review/beads-{fable,opus,astra,sol}.md)
Accounting corrections: the first review's verdict was 2 × BUILDABLE WITH GAPS (Fable, Opus) and 2 × NOT BUILDABLE (Astra, Sol), not a consensus; the orchestrator sides with NOT BUILDABLE after verification. The SDK premise was wrong: /home/master/p/fedimint's origin is upstream fedimint/fedimint, and upstream v0.12.0+ has single-attempt send dedup (703a37e8f3f) and component-wise fee limits (d5febdf9d37); spec-bsd and spec-ezl were closed as false, and ADR-0032 already says fork patches become requirements and SDK versions are a code-repo fact. title: SEC-25 seed encryption key source is an untaken decision: file it in chapter 11 now; slot layout, delivery channel and CNF-47 follow the ADR
description:
MAJOR (P1), DECISION-GATED. Rewritten 2026-09-23 after the second four-model bead review; this text replaces the original (whose title promised the ADR, the STO and the channel — all blocked on the decision).

**The defect (verified, 4/4 reviewers twice).** 07-security-requirements.md:101-126 (SEC-25): the seed MUST NOT be stored in plaintext, keyed from outside the store — but the key SOURCE is ADR-0026's recommendation, not its decision; SEC-25 is silent on it, and the encrypted slot's layout is deferred to a STO identifier that does not exist. 05:48-51 (STO-4) defers the same way. 08:19-24 (HST-2) owns the COMPLETE environment surface and 08:40-50 (HST-3) has five keys and MUST reject any other — no key-source row or key anywhere. 08:97-104 (HST-6) has no unseal step; HST-7 / ALC-40 require exit-and-supervisor-restart, which an interactive prompt cannot survive. 10:288-303 (CNF-47) and 00:116-120 (OVR-14) require an old build to fail on the re-encrypted store, which needs a discriminator no STO rule defines. 11-open-questions.md:16-34 does not list the decision, against AGENTS.md.

**Severity.** Major, not blocker: because SEC-25 is silent on the source, an OS key facility, a fixed-path key file or a TTY prompt is compliant today, so an implementation exists. What is impossible is interoperability of the slot between implementations and a portable CNF-47.

**Actionable NOW (this bead, only this).** The chapter-11 entry naming the decision: key source (ADR-0026 option-1 variants: env var naming a passphrase file, KMS reference, interactive unseal, OS keystore), provisioning, unavailable-key behaviour, restart expectations under HST-7/ALC-40's exit-and-restart model, whether an unattended unseal must succeed, and the standalone / `mnemonic` / `restore-mnemonic` need for the key. Plus a note in SEC-25 that the source is governed by that question. Do NOT add a sentence that HST-2/HST-3 are "extended by that decision" — while the decision is open the set stays silent (AGENTS.md).

**Blocked on the ADR (file as a new bead when decided).** STO-36 (next free STO; STO-32 withdrawn — verify) owns the slot bytes: version/discriminator, AEAD, nonce, ciphertext, AAD, and KDF parameters only if the source is a passphrase; the discriminator MUST make an old build fail to decode (BIP-39 accepts 16-32-byte entropy, so a bare 32-byte ciphertext would decode as a 24-word seed). Delivery surface: HST-2 row and/or HST-3 key AND the standalone flag in HST-10. An unseal step in HST-6 ("load the seed" may absorb it). CNF-47 restated with fixed vectors; its "when the build that predates SEC-25 starts on it" is implementation-relative (a greenfield implementation has no such build) — restate as "a wallet that reads the slot as plaintext entropy fails". Android's Keystore path (ADR-0011) is a second unowned mechanism — coordinate with spec-11k.

Owners: 11-open-questions.md, SEC-25 (the governing note). Depends on nothing.

title: OPS-45 pre-fund admission at the fourth killpoint can terminalize a committed send (Invoiced not exempt)
description:
BLOCKER, Astra, verified. 03-operation-lifecycle.md:259-264 (OPS-45): for Move and DirectInflow pre-fund admission runs BEFORE reassembly (OPS-20) and is skipped only when the cached record is trusted and its phase is Sending | Settled | Refunded | Failed | Stranded — Invoiced is not exempt. 03:100-103 (OPS-7): amount + fee_cap <= balance[from] - reservations.outbound(from), sampled fresh. 03:584 (OPS-28, fourth killpoint): send committed; the record lacks the send operation id — required resume is backfill, or a re-pay deduplicates to already in flight. 03:271-272: its refusal is Permanent and terminalizes the intent.
Scenario: a source holding just enough for amount + fee_cap; the send commits and debits it; the process dies before the send op id is written; on restart the record is Invoiced, OPS-45 runs the OPS-7 arithmetic on the debited balance, fails insufficient_after_reservations, and the intent is Failed while the outgoing contract is in flight. Contradicts OPS-28 exactly-once and CNF-12 (10:92).
Fix: for Move/DirectInflow run reassembly (discover committed artifacts by move_id / dedup) before pre-fund admission, or exempt Invoiced when the send is found committed; state which. Add a killpoint-4 scenario with a tightly funded source, once with the pre-receive draft cache present and once after cache loss.

## Review corrections (2026-09-23, four-model bead review: Fable, Opus, Astra, Sol)
CONFIRMED by all four; understated (Opus): a second trigger is the DESTINATION check — at killpoint 4 the swap may already have completed, so balance[to] already includes amount and OPS-7's 'balance[to] + reservations.inbound(to) + amount <= per_fed_cap' counts it twice (over_cap even with a well-funded source). DirectInflow has the same exposure: a crash after the invoice write but before the Awaiting write re-performs an Executing intent with cached phase Invoiced; if the payer already paid, the destination is double-counted. Corrected fix (one formulation, Sol; keyed on reassembled artifacts, not on the undefined 'trusted' — Fable, Opus): in OPS-45, for Move and DirectInflow run reassembly (OPS-20: cache, then the operation log by move_id / correlation key) BEFORE pre-fund admission; then skip the SOURCE arithmetic when the reassembled record has a send operation id (killpoints 2-3 still need it: the send is new funding), and skip the DESTINATION arithmetic when a receive artifact exists (invoice or receive operation id). Exempting every Invoiced record without the lookup is wrong (Astra): it would admit an unfunded invoice without the fresh checks. Owner OPS-45; OPS-19, OPS-7 ('again at perform time') and CONTEXT.md Reassembly keep citing it; OPS-35's optional pre-step backfill becomes irrelevant. Scenario here (not in the coverage bead): amend CNF-12 or add CNF-55 — killpoint 4 with a tight source, with the destination at cap minus amount, with the pre-receive draft cache present and lost.

## Second review (2026-09-23, four-model bead review round 2: Fable, Opus, Astra, Sol)
CONFIRMED (P0). Fold in the unfiled minor that lives next door: OPS-19 'share one plan and one step loop' is a code-structure sentence that fails the refactor test — reword to the shared observable semantics while editing OPS-45's neighbour. CNF-55 is the next free CNF (verify). spec-tc0 no longer lists OPS-45; the killpoint-4 scenario is this bead's alone. spec-bsk lands after this (the rewrite removes one 'trusted' use).

title: FMI-17 send dedup (and FMI-30/38/39/41) describe the fork SDK, not upstream: make the guarantees wallet-enforced
description:
BLOCKER, Astra + Opus, verified for FMI-17 against the local checkout. 02-fedimint-integration.md:235-237 (FMI-17): an lnv2 send is deduplicated by an operation id derived from the invoice: one payment attempt per invoice per client; a second send MUST NOT fund a second outgoing contract. 03:347 (raw pay) and 03:151-153 (OPS-10, retry refused with this invoice already consumed its single payment attempt) rest on it. The local fork (bradleystachurski/fedimint, modules/fedimint-lnv2-client/src/lib.rs:567-570) pins the attempt index to 0 with the comment that older clients derived a fresh index per payment attempt; upstream master derives OperationId from (invoice, attempt) and lets a failed/refunded attempt be followed by a new one. An implementer on the public SDK therefore funds a second contract after an unrecorded, later-refunded send — exactly what FMI-17 forbids — and never sees the dead operation the text promises.
Opus lists the other rules the withdrawn FMI-1 recorded as fork patches: FMI-30 (complete-or-fail within 600 s of no progress), FMI-38 (5-minute bounded re-issued waits), FMI-39 (single-share decryption), FMI-41 (claim retried until expiry). Each is a legitimate requirement but presupposes SDK behaviour the public SDK may not have.
Fix: (a) make the no-second-attempt guarantee a wallet rule: persist the operation id before issuing the send (already the raw path's order) and refuse a second send of any invoice that has a recorded operation id regardless of the terminal, including after a missing artifact write; state the disposition of terminal failed/refunded sends explicitly; (b) a chapter-02 note (or a row per rule) naming which FMI behaviours an upstream SDK may not provide, so an implementer knows to enforce them above the SDK; (c) a restart scenario: send issued, artifact write lost, send refunded, restart — no second contract.
close_reason: Premise false (Opus, Astra, Sol; re-verified against /home/master/p/fedimint whose origin is upstream fedimint/fedimint): single-attempt lnv2 send dedup is upstream since v0.12.0 (commit 703a37e8f3f, 2026-07-10); the code repo's pin 72b1e5be has it too. FMI-17 and OPS-17 describe the public SDK. FMI-30/38/39/41 are already MUSTs on the wallet; whether an SDK release provides them is a code-repo finding, and a chapter-02 SDK-version note would fail the refactor test (ADR-0032). The fix's claim that the raw path persists the op id before the send was also wrong (OPS-17: issue, then persist; the hash lookup covers the crash window). Residual: FMI-17 says 'the protocol derives' where it is the client that derives (wording nit); the send-issued / artifact-lost / refunded / restart scenario moves to the coverage bead.

title: Gross-up: FMI-18 selects an over-crediting contract, FMI-15 says never more and misstates what the receive quote covers; OPS-44 cites a nonexistent fixed point
description:
MAJOR (P1). Rewritten 2026-09-23 after the second four-model bead review; this text replaces the original and the merged spec-pcr text (both premises were partly wrong, see below).

**The contradiction (verified).** 02-fedimint-integration.md:213-219 (FMI-15): the destination is credited "never more, and possibly less by a bounded shortfall … the best verified under-crediting candidate". 02:267-268 (FMI-18): `gross_up(net, gateway_fee, fed_fee)` is "the smallest invoice amount such that `contract = invoice − gw(invoice)` and `contract − fed(contract) ≥ net`" — the `≥` selects the OVER-crediting side when the step function has no exact solution, the case FMI-15 expressly contemplates. 03:449-450 (OPS-44) cites "(`FMI-18`, `OPS-22`'s fixed point)"; OPS-22 (03:502-513) defines no fixed point — the phrase exists only in CONTEXT.md:128-129 (Delivered net). OPS-23 (03:536) checks only equality of quoted and committed contracts, so it cannot catch an over-crediting quote.

**A false protocol statement in the set (verified at the pin 72b1e5be and at upstream master).** FMI-15:218 says the federation's "mint output fee on the claim" is one "which the lnv2 receive quote does not include". That is wrong: `receive_fee_quote` (modules/fedimint-lnv2-client/src/lib.rs:827 at the pin) calls `Client::fee_quote`, which "runs the exact same primary-module balancing (`create_final_inputs_and_outputs` …)" and whose result covers the Lightning input fee, the mint change-output fees and sub-denomination dust; only the gateway's off-chain fee is excluded. So the merged spec-pcr premise ("delivered net omits the mint output fee") was false, and the round-1 formula `credited = invoice − receive_quote − mint_fee` would subtract the mint fee twice. Do not use it.

**The real residual (Opus, verified).** The federation quote is "point-in-time: it depends on the current inventory" (client.rs:814); the mint lays out change against the wallet's note inventory at CLAIM time, and the per-note fee applies per change note. The quote is taken when the invoice is minted; the claim is priced when it lands. So the credited amount can differ from `invoice − receive_quote` in EITHER direction, and "never more" cannot be guaranteed at mint time unless the mint's per-note fee is zero.

**Fix, one owner each.**
- FMI-15 owns the vocabulary, defined once: requested net `N`; invoice `I`; gateway receive fee `G(I)`; incoming contract `C = I − G(I)`; federation receive quote `F(C)` = the whole claim transaction's fee as quoted at mint time (Lightning input fee + mint output fees + dust — say so, and delete the "does not include" clause); **delivered net** `= C − F(C)` as quoted (this is what `receive_quote` already means in OPS-18/OPS-44: "`actual = amount − committed + the federation's receive quote on committed`", "`delivered = invoice − receive_quote`"); **credited** = what the balance actually rose by. "Never more" binds the delivered net. State the credited-vs-delivered variance bound (the mint's per-note fee × the change-note-count difference) or state that the set does not bound it.
- FMI-18 owns the gross-up contract: the exact solution when one exists, else the candidate whose quoted delivered net is the largest not exceeding `N`, ties to the smallest invoice; the shortfall bound (one receive-fee step); the no-solution case; the 5 000 msat minimum-contract case by citation to FMI-16 (OPS-22 already maps it to `Permanent("direct inflow amount too small: …")` — keep and cite). Correct the inequality.
- OPS-44 drops "OPS-22's fixed point"; CONTEXT.md:128-131 aligns (it says "Every ENFORCED fee cap is computed from the delivered net", which contradicts OVR-7's funding-move planned-cap exception at 00:57-59 — OVR-7 owns, the glossary cites). OVR-7's "what the destination is actually credited" becomes "the delivered net (FMI-15)"; ALC-21's `invoice − receive_quote` IS the delivered net, no change of basis needed. executive-summary.md:62-63 and :73-75 restate the same rules — cite.
- Scenarios: the environment header (10:26-27 "'rises by the amount' … are exact"), CNF-9 (already "minus the gateway and federation receive fees"), CNF-11 (10:87-88), CNF-12 (10:95), CNF-13, CNF-42 (10:155 asserts "exactly once" — multiplicity, not amount; leave) assert exact credits with no fee fixture. Either fix the environment's mint per-note fee at zero and say so in the header (then delivered = credited and the exact assertions hold), or assert the delivered net at the ledger (STO-17 stamps it) and bound the balance change by CNF-10's rule. CNF-10's "at most 1 000 msat less" gets the same treatment.

Owners: FMI-15, FMI-18; cite from OVR-7, ALC-21, OPS-22/23/24/44, CNF-9/10/11/12/13. Hand-off (done-condition 6): none for the pin — the pin already quotes this way; the spec text was the error.

Depends on nothing. spec-bqv (route cost) and spec-tc0's exact-credit assertions depend on this vocabulary.

title: OPS-10 lets a 'send failed:' move be retried (double-send); older attempts are unaddressable by API-42
description:
BLOCKER (P0). Rewritten 2026-09-23 after the second four-model bead review; this text replaces the original and its round-1 correction (they disagreed on every point). The claimability half lives in spec-u3u — do not duplicate it here.

**The defect (verified).** 03-operation-lifecycle.md:151-163 (OPS-10): retry is refused only for "a `Failed` pay that recorded an operation id" and "a `Failed` move whose move record's phase is `Stranded`"; the retry write "deletes the cached move record, appends a fresh ledger row and repoints the key index". 02:328-335 (FMI-37) case (b): after `send failed:` the wallet "cannot tell" whether the outgoing contract was funded. 04-api-contract.md:580-584 (API-42): `{key}` names "the operation whose contract reached a terminal non-claim" — after a retry the key resolves to the new attempt. So: a move whose send reached the SDK's terminal `Failure` (OPS-27 maps `Failed(msg) → Failed` without awaiting the receive) can be retried by the user, which mints a new invoice and sends AGAIN while attempt 0's outgoing contract may be funded and attempt 0's receive state machine is still running in the destination client (it claims if funded). That is a double-send under OVR-2's exactly-once property. HST-32's evidence preservation covers only `Stranded`.

**Guard — decided, do not re-derive.** A `Failed` move or direct inflow whose error begins `send failed:` (the prefix HST-32 fixes) is NEVER retryable, exactly like `Stranded`: refused `conflict`, with a named message (e.g. "this move's send reached a terminal failure; its outgoing contract's position is unknown"), classified by OPS-39/API-6 as 409. Reasons this is permanent, not "until the position is known": after the SDK's terminal `Failure` (`FinalSendOperationState ∈ Success | Refunded | Failure`) the send state machine never runs again and no verb in the set reads an outgoing contract's position afterwards; a verifying preimage (FMI-23) proves PAYMENT and must forbid a new send, never release the guard (Astra); only authoritative evidence of no funding or a completed refund could ever justify a new payment, and the set has no reader for it. A fresh key (a new occurrence or nonce) is always available and mints a fresh invoice. Note direct inflows have no outgoing send: the `send failed:` rule does not apply to them; a `receive failed:` direct inflow stays retryable, but its old funded contract must remain addressable (below).

**Older-attempt addressability.** "Orphans the contract" was overstated: OPS-10 keeps "two truthful rows", STO-15 keeps the operation ids in them, STO-20 keeps older rows addressable by `seq`, and the client operation log survives. What is missing is a wire contract for API-42 to address an older attempt. Lighter than an attempt-scoped record key (a new tag would break STO-5's "exactly thirteen tags"): API-42 locates the receive operation by the attempt correlation keys in the operation log (STO-34: the key, then `retry:<len>:<key>:<n>`). DECIDE THE SHAPE in the bead's edit — API-42 returns one `outcome`, so state whether `reclaim {key}` addresses the newest attempt's contract, every attempt's unclaimed contract, or one attempt named by a new parameter (a wire change to API-42 and CNF-26, and to the CLI verb — spec-ee9 depends on it). Applies to moves, direct inflows and raw receives alike.

**Owners.** OPS-10 (the refusal and the retry write), STO-34 (correlation keys), API-42 (addressing), HST-32 (evidence). Scenario here: a `send failed:` move → retry refused 409 with the message; a `receive failed:` direct inflow retried → the old attempt's contract still addressable by reclaim.

Depends on spec-u3u (what API-42 may claim is settled there first; both edit API-42's precondition). spec-5gn, spec-ee9 and the retry-artifacts bead depend on this one.

title: OPS-18 over-cap raw receive publishes its invoice before the Permanent outcome lands; OPS-16 / API-21 return it as payable
description:
MAJOR (P1). Rewritten 2026-09-23 after the second four-model bead review; this text replaces the original (which cited OPS-22 — the rule is OPS-18) and its round-1 correction.

**The defect (verified).** 03-operation-lifecycle.md:385-388 (OPS-18, raw Receive committed-fee check): "`actual > fee_cap` → persist the operation id and invoice **first**, so the orphan is recorded, then `Permanent(…)`". 03:302-304 (OPS-16): the invoice target resolves "as soon as the intent's invoice or the move record's invoice exists". 04-api-contract.md:297-299 (API-21): 409 `failed` only for a terminal intent WITHOUT an invoice, and "Re-submitting the same key re-yields the same invoice (OPS-8)". OPS-13: a fenced write that applies "wakes every waiter parked on the key"; API-21 blocks "up to 30 seconds for the invoice artifact". So the artifact write wakes the waiters and the payer receives an invoice the wallet has already judged over cap, BEFORE the `Permanent` outcome lands, and again on every resubmission; meanwhile the terminalized intent releases its reservation (OPS-9 reserves only non-terminal intents) while the invoice stays payable for up to 3 600 s.

**Fix — pick ONE publication rule and state it; the two candidates:**
- (preferred, no new field, mirrors the move path) OPS-24 already says a refused receive "MUST NOT take the invoice, which is never surfaced". Apply the same to the raw receive: OPS-18 records the operation id (the orphan) and its `Failed` disposition in ONE transaction (STO-16 already puts the ledger row in the same transaction as any status change), and does NOT publish the invoice: OPS-16's invoice target resolves only for a non-`Failed` intent, and waiters woken by that write see a terminal without an invoice, so API-21's existing 409 rule is already right. Publication eligibility and artifact visibility are then atomic; "check status after an earlier artifact write" does NOT close the race (Astra).
- (alternative) keep recording the invoice but make API-21 answer 409 for a `Failed` intent whatever artifacts it holds. NOT "any terminal intent": `Done` must keep re-yielding its invoice (API-21, OPS-8).

**Consequences to state, not ask.** (i) The orphan, if paid out of band, is claimed by the SDK's own receive state machine for that operation (`Pending → Claiming → Claimed`, verified at the pin and master); the wallet initiates nothing; the only accounting question is that the `Failed` row keeps its error while the balance rises — say the ledger keeps the failure evidence and FMI-41's re-claim covers a rejected claim. With the preferred rule this cannot happen unless the wallet leaked the invoice. (ii) Retry: OPS-10 refuses only a `Failed` PAY that recorded an operation id, so this `Failed` receive IS retryable, and it mints a second invoice while the orphan is live — decide whether OPS-10 refuses a `Failed` receive that recorded an operation id, symmetric with pay, or allows it with the older contract addressable by API-42 (spec-cuw's addressing). The separate defect that a retry RE-ADOPTS the old operation id has its own bead.

Owners: OPS-18, OPS-16, API-21; OPS-10 for the retry decision. Scenarios here: a waiter already attached when the over-cap outcome is recorded receives 409, not the invoice; re-submission of the failed key → 409; a retry with the older invoice still payable.

Depends on spec-cuw (the retry/addressing decision). The paid-orphan dependency on spec-u3u was dropped: the SDK claims on its own.

title: Supersession marker: OPS-31 says the retired parent keeps it, CNF-24 asserts it is cleared
description:
MAJOR, Astra, verified. 03-operation-lifecycle.md:617-620 (OPS-31): the marker is cleared by ... the exchange (the retired parent keeps it). 10-conformance-checklist.md:145-147 (CNF-24): the parent is Failed as superseded with its marker cleared. 01-domain-model.md:181 requires preservation of the parent's evidence.
Fix: choose one persisted-state contract. Evidence preservation argues for: the parent keeps the marker, inactive because the row is terminal; the child never inherits it. Say it once in OPS-31, make CNF-24 assert exactly that, and test retained evidence separately from active status.

## Review corrections (2026-09-23, four-model bead review: Fable, Opus, Astra, Sol)
CONFIRMED by all four; the resolution stands (parent keeps the field, inactive because terminal; child never inherits it; API-33's evacuation_refusal_active already implies the field survives). One addition (Astra): fix OPS-31's projection too — it currently yields false for a readable intent WITHOUT a marker and leaves a terminal intent WITH retained evidence uncovered; align with API-33: true only for the live Pending evacuation carrying the marker, false for every other readable intent, omitted only when no intent is readable. CNF-24's assertion lands here, not in the coverage bead. DOM-20, STO-25 align.

## Second review (2026-09-23, four-model bead review round 2: Fable, Opus, Astra, Sol)
CONFIRMED. The sentence to rewrite is OPS-31's own 'cleared by … the exchange (the retired parent keeps it)', which contradicts itself; OPS-31:626-628's three-case projection ('true for an exact readable Pending agent Evacuate with a marker, false for an exact readable intent without one, omitted when no intent is readable') has no case for a Failed parent WITH a retained marker — align to API-33:461 ('false = the intent is readable but not live'). The evidence survives in the STO-25 sidecar (refusal) whichever way the marker goes, so 'evidence preservation' does not force 'keep'; keeping is simply the reading that matches OPS-31's parenthetical and API-33. Align DOM-20/STO-25. The CNF-24 assertion is this bead's alone.

title: Send fee admission is not bound to the contract actually funded: the SDK re-reads routing_info inside send; OPS-29 must state the property
description:
BLOCKER (P0). Rewritten 2026-09-23 after the second four-model bead review; this text replaces the original and its round-1 correction. Loss is bounded (by FMI-19's envelope, 100 sat + 1.5 %, per payment), never principal; P0 stands because no compliant implementation exists on the presupposed SDK without a patch.

**SDK facts — verified at the pin 72b1e5be, v0.12.1 and upstream master.** `send(invoice, gateway, custom_meta)` (modules/fedimint-lnv2-client/src/lib.rs:574-590 at the pin) re-reads `routing_info` inside the call, computes `send_parameters(&invoice)` from what it read then, and funds `send_fee.add_to(amount)` at those terms; nothing the wallet passes bounds it. `send_with_terms` (upstream 9120506f70d / merged 2eed40ae3ef, 2026-09-10; refuses ANY change of the (fee, expiration-delta) tuple, cheaper included, with `TermsChanged`) exists on master only, in no tag.

**The defect in the set (verified).** 03-operation-lifecycle.md:557 (move send step) and 03:353 (raw pay) run the cap check on the QUOTE, then issue the send. 07-security-requirements.md:164 (SEC-7) distinguishes wallet caps from the protocol schedule limits. A gateway can quote within the wallet's cap and then raise its fee within FMI-19's protocol envelope before the send reads it; the funded contract exceeds what was admitted, and nothing in the set forbids it.

**Fix — one property, one owner.** The spec cannot command an SDK method; it states the PROPERTY. Choose ONE of the two acceptance policies and write it (do not write both — they differ): (A) the fee the funded outgoing contract carries, plus the federation's send quote on it, MUST fit the admitted cap, or nothing is funded; (B) the routing terms the send funds under MUST equal the terms admitted, or nothing is funded (upstream's `send_with_terms` policy). Recommend (A): it is what the cap means and does not fail on a cheaper re-quote. Say whether the expiration delta (a lock-time term, not a fee) is bound. Class: `Retryable` with a re-quote, consistent with OPS-26's total-over-cap `Retryable`; preserve raw Pay's and the move send-leg's existing terminal semantics. Owner: OPS-29 (the rule that says where caps bind; SEC-7 cites it) — decided, do not re-open; OPS-17 (pay) and OPS-26 (move send) cite it; FMI-17's refusal table gains a "terms changed → `Retryable`, nothing funded" row only as a citation of OPS-29. Amend ADR-0030:62-65 with a dated note: its residual ("the cap bounds what the wallet knowingly agrees to, not what such a gateway does afterwards") already concerns an unvetted gateway and stays; the sentence "Vetting is what normally covers that" is false (vetting binds nothing about fees) — strike it; one ADR-0030 amendment, coordinated with spec-y0b.

**Scenario here (not in the coverage bead):** a gateway raises its fee between the quote and the send; the wallet funds nothing; the intent is `Retryable`, and the next attempt re-quotes. Chapter 10 forbids marking a scenario with a result (10:5-7 "A scenario carries no result"), so do NOT mark it as failing.

**Hand-off (done-condition 6):** the pinned SDK cannot satisfy the property without a terms-bound send; the reference implementation fails this scenario until it vendors or upgrades. Record in the code repository's open findings.

title: Delivered net omits the mint output fee FMI-15 admits; CNF-11 demands an exact credit with no fee fixture
description:
MAJOR, Astra, PLAUSIBLE. 06-allocator-and-automation.md:297 defines delivered net as invoice - receive_quote, what the destination is actually credited; 03:454 (OPS-44) sizes and enforces the cap on that arithmetic. 02-fedimint-integration.md:218 (FMI-15) admits the federation's mint output fee on the claim, which the lnv2 receive quote does not include. So the computed delivered net can exceed the real credit. 10-conformance-checklist.md:79 (CNF-10) tolerates a bounded shortfall while 10:87 (CNF-11) requires B to rise by exactly the amount, under an environment (10:20-27) that fixes no fee schedule.
Fix: define requested, quoted and credited amounts once and use the right one in each rule (cap enforcement on the quoted delivered net is fine if stated; balance assertions on the credited amount); rewrite CNF-11's assertion as a bound, or fix the fixture's fees so exactly is true, and say so.
close_reason: Merged into spec-1nc (one fee/credit arithmetic change, one owner) on all four reviewers' recommendation.

title: Attempt-fence outcome class drifts: OPS-10/OPS-13 say Retryable, STO-9/OPS-43 say Permanent, OPS-4 forbids Failed
description:
MAJOR, Fable, verified by quote. 03-operation-lifecycle.md:162-164 (OPS-10): every durable writer is attempt-fenced: a write by a stale attempt writes nothing, and a drive treats that as Retryable; 03:199-201 (OPS-13) the same for every artifact write. 05-persistence.md:186-190 (STO-9): the admission insert, a plain status write and the retryable reset report a differing stored attempt as a Permanent error; 03:256-257 (OPS-43): the reset requires the current Executing attempt, else Permanent. 03:54-58 (OPS-4): a journal failure MUST NOT produce a Failed intent. The class an implementer records, and the ledger error string (STO-35), differ by which rule is followed.
Fix: STO-9 owns it — a fenced write writes nothing and reports not-applied; a drive treats not-applied as Retryable and terminalizes nothing — and OPS-10, OPS-13, OPS-43 cite it.

## Review corrections (2026-09-23, four-model bead review: Fable, Opus, Astra, Sol)
DOWNGRADED to minor (Opus: reconcilable as written; Fable, Astra: no behavioural divergence; Sol: real but the OPS-4 appeal is misattributed). STO-9 already splits fenced writes into two groups (05:186-190): the admission insert, plain status write and retryable reset 'report a differing stored attempt as a Permanent error' (a STORAGE error class, STO-7), and 'every other fenced write … writes nothing and reports that it did not apply', which is what OPS-10/OPS-13's Retryable refers to. OPS-4 rules the first group ('terminalizes nothing … MUST NOT produce a Failed intent'). Nothing reaches the ledger error. Residual: 'Permanent' names both a storage error class and a perform outcome, and OPS-43's 'else Permanent' reads as the latter. Fix: a wording change in STO-9 — 'a stale-attempt refusal, never a perform outcome' — and OPS-43 cites it. Do NOT re-class the reset (STO-8 relies on 'Permanent on a failed guard').

## Second review (2026-09-23, four-model bead review round 2: Fable, Opus, Astra, Sol)
CONFIRMED, P2. The permanent failed-attempt guard is in STO-9, not STO-8 (fix the citation). The chapter-05 introduction says 'Retryable and Permanent are the outcome classes of 03', so the storage-result vs drive-disposition distinction must be WRITTEN there, not assumed: a stale writer produces no mutation, and the caller's resulting disposition is unambiguous (STO-9, OPS-10/13/43).

title: FMI-40 private-network gateway allowance has no home: add a walletd.toml key / standalone flag, default off
description:
MAJOR, Fable + Opus, verified. 02-fedimint-integration.md:138-152 (FMI-40): MUST treat as unavailable — without connecting — a loopback, RFC 1918 or unique-local host; a host MAY offer an explicit configuration that permits private-network gateways — a test environment's gateways are on loopback — and that configuration MUST default to off. 08-hosts-and-deployment.md:19-24 (HST-2) and 08:40-50 (HST-3, five keys, MUST reject any other) leave no place for it. 10:20-27 puts every conformance gateway on a vetted list; 07:218-219 (SEC-18) says the build a scenario runs on is the implementation's own. On a release build every local harness gateway is unavailable and no money scenario can pass.
Fix: a sixth HST-3 key (and the standalone flag in HST-10), default off, named in FMI-40; or state in chapter 10's environment that gateways are reachable at public addresses.

## Review corrections (2026-09-23, four-model bead review: Fable, Opus, Astra, Sol)
DOWNGRADED to minor and RECAST (Astra, Sol: FMI-40 says a host 'MAY offer' the configuration, and chapter 10 does not require loopback gateways, so no contradiction exists and 'no money scenario can pass' was an unstated harness assumption; Fable, Opus kept major on the practical ground that every local harness is loopback). If the product offers private-network gateways, the switch needs a home — a named HST-3 key (e.g. allow_private_gateways, default off), the standalone flag in the CLI grammar (spec-ee9), FMI-40 naming the owner and keeping 'MUST NOT affect the link-local and metadata rule'; its scope must match whatever spec-22p decides (gateways only, or every egress class). Fold the decision into spec-22p's list; nothing else to do here until it is taken.
close_reason: Merged into spec-22p (Fable, Opus, Astra: an open bead with 'nothing to do until the decision is taken' misleads the ready queue). Residual carried by spec-22p: FMI-40's 'A host MAY offer an explicit configuration that permits private-network gateways' is a MAY no compliant host can exercise, because HST-2 owns the complete environment surface and HST-3 has five keys and MUST reject any other; spec-22p either files the chapter-11 entry for that allowance or strikes the MAY.

title: Discovery sources cannot be configured: FMI-28's {base} comes from nowhere; STO-15 has a Nostr source ALC-28 never collects
description:
MAJOR, Opus, verified. 02-fedimint-integration.md:433-434 (FMI-28): GET {base}/federations — nothing says where {base} comes from or how many Observer sources exist. 06-allocator-and-automation.md:396 (ALC-28) collects from Observer, Manual; what a Manual source is and where its invites come from is unstated. 05-persistence.md:298 (STO-15) has DiscoverySource in {Observer, Nostr, Manual} — Nostr is collected by nothing. ## Second review (2026-09-23, four-model bead review round 2: Fable, Opus, Astra, Sol)
CONFIRMED. The original's option to drop the Nostr source is WITHDRAWN (Sol: the original and the round-1 correction conflict); act on the correction — Nostr is persisted vocabulary under OVR-14/DOM-12/FMI-43. Design input: the reference CLI's discover takes --source, a base URL flag defaulting to https://observer.fedimint.org/api, and --invite for Manual — the default-Observer product decision is already taken by the implementation and needs ratifying or refusing in chapter 11 (ADR-0019:35-36 leaves it open), not inventing. If the choice is Policy fields, every fixed count moves with it: DOM-15 'twenty-eight parameters', STO-13, API-20 (twice), API-27, CNF-26 'each of the twenty-eight flags', STO-30's decode-when-absent list and its counts ('fourteen in the journal … eighteen'). title: Standing-instruction acknowledgement is 'decided' (ch. 11, ADR-0014) but no requirement records or gates on it: DOM-22 owns it
description:
MAJOR (P1 — not P0: no requirement in 00-10 states the acknowledgement as a MUST, so a compliant wallet exists today; the defect is a missing requirement). Rewritten 2026-09-23 after the second four-model bead review; this text replaces the original and its round-1 correction (whose "stronger finding" about open question 1 was wrong).

**The defect (verified).** 11-open-questions.md:18-25 (question 1): "that acknowledgement is decided and not in question"; docs/adr/0014:10-13: "an explicit, plain-language, gating acknowledgement BEFORE any funds are received"; CONTEXT.md:281-289 calls it recorded. The complete API table (04:100), the fresh-admission checks (03:77, OPS-6) and the complete journal tag table (05:77) supply no acceptance operation, no durable acknowledgement and no enforcement check. The seeded policy row CANNOT be the acknowledgement: `init` creates it automatically; do not replace consent with initialization, and do not fabricate acceptance on migration.

**What question 1 actually asks — leave it alone.** Chapter 11 says: "What is undecided is whether automated management is the onboarding flow's default posture — the acknowledgement presented to every user, declined to opt out — or an option a user turns on" and "nothing about which flow presents it". That an always-running scheduler exists on walletd (HST-6, ALC-42) does not answer the presentation/default-on question. Do not reword question 1 to the scheduler, and do not narrow it to Android without spec-11k's scope decision.

**Fix.** A domain owner for the acknowledgement (DOM-22, next free DOM — verify) defining: content (what is acknowledged, in plain language), explicit acceptance, durable state, the inbound admission gate (which operations OPS-5/OPS-6 refuse before it and with which OPS-39 reason), behaviour on fresh stores, existing stores, recovery and restart, and host applicability. Name each surface it touches instead of leaving them to the agent: storage (a new journal tag breaks STO-5's "exactly thirteen tags" and every count after it; a `WatchState` field goes through STO-30 — pick one and say which), the route and verb (API-8's "nineteen routes", API-26, the CLI grammar), and the chapter-10 environment ("a wallet joined to A and B …" must now include the acknowledgement or every money scenario is refused). Say whether a user `join` counts as "funds received" (ADR-0014: "BEFORE any funds are received"). Name the natural gate option so the agent does not refuse user receives by default: the set already has a non-money cycle (ALC-47: "no tick row, no route pricing, no commit and no fresh probe") and a readiness vocabulary (ALC-45); an un-acknowledged store can run every cycle as non-money with a new `automation_blocked` reason, leaving `receive`/`pay` untouched — whether ADR-0014 means "gate receives" or "gate the agent" is the product decision, and it goes into the DOM-22 wording as an explicit choice, not the agent's judgement.

Owners: DOM-22 (new), with STO/API/OPS-5 citing. Depends on nothing; coordinate with spec-11k (host applicability) and spec-iym.

title: Android host is presupposed by prose and ADRs but specified nowhere: one scope sentence in OVR-1, aligned prose, note on ADR-0032
description:
MINOR (P2). Rewritten 2026-09-23 after the second four-model bead review; this text replaces the original and its round-1 correction (which sent the work to chapter 11 — the wrong home).

**What is real (verified).** 00-overview.md:23-26 (OVR-1): "The hosts and frontends a compliant wallet provides, and the contract of each, are 08-hosts-and-deployment.md" — and chapter 08 specifies walletd, standalone, the CLI and the sidecar only. executive-summary.md:18-22 ("embedded in hosts: … and an Android app"), CONTEXT.md:56-60 and :373-376 (Host, Silent backup: "the Android app on a phone"), ADR-0003 (Block Store recovery), ADR-0011 (Keystore, biometric-to-send), ADR-0031 (in-process engine, WorkManager wakes) and ADR-0032:17-18 ("the hosts (a daemon, an Android app, a browser sidecar, wasm where named)") all treat Android as part of the product. So the compliance scope (OVR-1) is explicit and no implementation is non-compliant for lacking an Android host — a prose inconsistency, minor.

**Why not chapter 11.** AGENTS.md sends "a product decision nobody has taken" to chapter 11. Android being part of the product IS taken (three accepted ADRs and ADR-0032). What is missing is requirements, which is spec work, not an open product question. No new ADR is needed to say the set does not yet specify the Android host: that restates OVR-1 and supersedes nothing.

**Fix (this bead).** One sentence in OVR-1 (the owner): this version of the set specifies the server hosts and the CLI; the Android host's contract (ADR-0003/0011/0031) is not yet specified and nothing in chapters 00-10 binds it. Bring the executive summary and CONTEXT.md's Host / Silent backup entries into line, citing OVR-1. Add a dated note on ADR-0032:17 that the Android host is presupposed but its HST contract is pending. Coordinate with spec-dn8 (the acknowledgement's host applicability) and spec-iym (Keystore is a second key-source mechanism).

**Not this bead.** Writing the Android contract (HST-34+, next free HST: observable key protection, authentication gates, backup/recovery, lifecycle and wakes, restart/failure, engine ownership, without JNI/WorkManager mechanism, plus scenarios) is a separate future bead; file it when the host is scheduled.

Owner: OVR-1. Depends on nothing.

title: Evacuation hop routing is owned by the glossary and ADR-0029 only; no FMI/OPS rule, no deadline, no hop scenario
description:
MAJOR, 4/4 reviewers, verified. CONTEXT.md:223-241 (Shared route / Hop) states the loop normatively: ranked together, cheapest composed cost among different-node combinations first, the next tried when the first sizes to nothing viable, a failed hop sets aside that node pair. docs/adr/0029:50-84 gives the composed-cost formula, tie-break (lower receive fee, then the ordered pair of URLs) and per-attempt deadline — by function name (quote_fresh_send_required_cost, FreshMoveCost::total_fee), which fails the refactor test. 00-overview.md:104-108 (OVR-13) and 02:197-201 (FMI-14) say in ADR-0029's order; 03:435-440 (OPS-21) snapshots one gateway fee per leg without saying how the two gateways are chosen; 02:282-297 (FMI-22) bounds the fallback scan at 10 s and names no bound for the class scan. Chapter 10 cites OVR-13 zero times: the environment (10:20-27) always has a shared gateway G, CNF-14 uses it, CNF-53 is one break-glass gateway — a shared-route-only implementation passes.
Fix: FMI-44 (or extend FMI-14): candidate set = validated destination list x validated source list on distinct lightning_public_key; order by composed cost at the ask (ALC-13's formula), ties by lower receive fee then URL pair; next combination on an empty sizing result; one per-attempt deadline named in FMI-22; what journaled as truncated writes. CONTEXT.md and ADR-0029 cite it. Add a CNF with disjoint vetted lists on distinct Lightning nodes asserting route identities, both fee legs, committed-route replay and fallback after a failed performer.

## Review corrections (2026-09-23, four-model bead review: Fable, Opus, Astra, Sol)
CONFIRMED by all four; the fix needs more decisions named. (1) The proposed cost formula was WRONG (Astra): ADR-0029:54 requires the FULL route cost including the federation quotes on the contracts gross-up implies (FMI-18/OPS-44), not ALC-13's planning model — rank by the actual composed cost, then the accepted tie-breaks. (2) The shared class's own candidate loop for an EVACUATION (amount sized, not final; 'try a candidate, size it, on nothing viable try the next, then the next class') — FMI-14's steps are written for a final amount. (3) The per-attempt deadline must be a named constant in FMI-22, because 'inside perform_timeout' is undefined when the timeout is 0 (Opus); its relation to the perform budget; what a truncated search writes to the ledger row (a warning, an error text, nothing). (4) Which route's samples become the OPS-31 marker when both classes refuse (decides ALC-23 qualification). (5) A hop hint cannot be carried: Evacuate has one gateway? field (DOM-7) while the glossary says a hop hint is two identities — say so. (6) Cache-loss replay for hops: in STO-33 gateway names the gateway for THAT leg, so OPS-20 must reconstruct destination and source roles explicitly, never an undifferentiated newest gateway. (7) Set-aside (FMI-42) and the prohibition on switching after commitment. (8) The attempt-level sense of 'serves' ('serves this attempt') lives here (spec-hrb). Correct executive-summary.md:64-65, which says an ordinary move hops. FMI-44 only if no earlier FMI lands first. The hop CNF lands HERE: disjoint vetted lists on distinct Lightning nodes, cache loss both before and after the send record exists, route identities, both fee legs, fallback after a failed performer. Depends on spec-1nc (the composed cost uses the settled amount contract).

## Second review (2026-09-23, four-model bead review round 2: Fable, Opus, Astra, Sol)
CONFIRMED; large (the one bead a fresh agent needs a plan for). Additions: (1) executive-summary.md:34-35 ('through one gateway that serves both federations or two when none does') also says an ordinary move hops, beside 64-65 — fix both. (2) ADR-0029:75-79's 'ONE per-attempt deadline … far enough inside perform_timeout' becomes an FMI-22 row. (3) Specify the FAILURE TRANSITIONS, not only pricing and order (Astra): which failures abandon only the current candidate, advance from shared routing to a hop, end the attempt Retryable, supply structural refusal evidence, or set an endpoint/route aside; and that the shared-route search cannot consume the whole budget before the required hop fallback. (4) DOM-7's Evacuate {…, gateway?, …} is one field while CONTEXT.md:200-201 says a hint 'names a whole route … two gateway identities for a hop'; ALC-17 only ever stamps the pair's resolved_gateway, so a hop hint is never produced — delete the glossary sentence. FMI-44 is the next free FMI (highest defined 43; verify). Land after spec-shy (FMI-14 step 2's hint fallback is reused by the class loop) and spec-1nc (the composed cost is defined through FMI-18's gross-up); spec-hrb ('serves this attempt') and spec-y0b's hop note land after this. The OPS-20 hop-replay item is independent and may be split off.

title: ALC-39 sleeps on meta_module_expiry_secs, which FMI-3 and FMI-26 say is not an input
description:
MAJOR, 4/4 reviewers, verified. 06-allocator-and-automation.md:615-617 (ALC-39): the expiry deadlines are, per probed federation, only the corroborated config_expiry_secs and meta_module_expiry_secs (FMI-26). 02-fedimint-integration.md:405-406 (FMI-26): the meta module's consensus value is not an input (FMI-3); 02:32 (FMI-3): the meta module is not consumed. Neither name is defined anywhere, and the config expiry is trusted, not corroborated, in FMI-26's own taxonomy.
Fix: restate ALC-39 in FMI-26's vocabulary (the at-join config federation_expiry_timestamp, and a /status shutdown corroborated by f+1 peers, when in the future) and drop the meta-module deadline; or define the signal in FMI-26 and withdraw the not-consumed sentences.

## Review corrections (2026-09-23, four-model bead review: Fable, Opus, Astra, Sol)
CONFIRMED by all four; option 1 corrected (Opus, Astra, Sol): the /status scheduled_shutdown carries a SESSION INDEX ('whatever session index it names', FMI-26:416-417), not a time, and a corroborated signal schedules at once — it cannot be a sleep deadline, and ALC-39 already excludes 'the /status flag'. The deadline set is therefore exactly the at-join config federation_expiry_timestamp (FMI-26), when in the future; the override-meta wake stays in ALC-39's last sentence as a wake, never a deadline. Remove meta_module_expiry_secs and the undefined config_expiry_secs name. Owner ALC-39.

## Second review (2026-09-23, four-model bead review round 2: Fable, Opus, Astra, Sol)
CONFIRMED (P1 kept; P2 defensible: the evacuation trigger is FMI-26's and runs every cycle, the sleep deadline only moves a wake by at most one base_interval_secs). One sentence further (Astra): ALC-39 also says 'a wake re-adds the hinted expiry, recomputes the sleep' — as written a wake can put an override-served hint back into the deadline set the corrected sentence excludes; distinguish a wake NOTIFICATION from an admitted trusted deadline. While rewriting the sentence, replace 'per probed federation' with 'per snapshot federation' (spec-bsk lands after this).

title: FMI-19 component-wise fee limit has no wallet-side enforcer; OPS-21 and ADR-0029 say the protocol refuses lexicographically
description:
MAJOR, Opus + Sol, verified. 02-fedimint-integration.md:273-280 (FMI-19): a schedule above the limit MUST be refused; above is component-wise ... never a lexicographic comparison; this is an admission filter on the posted schedule; the class each refusal takes is FMI-16's and FMI-17's. 03:439-440 (OPS-21): warning, never refusing, on a schedule outside FMI-19's limits (the protocol refuses at the send). docs/adr/0029:26-29: the SDK's limits bound each leg's BASE but not the ppm because PaymentFee compares lexicographically. FMI-17 classes gateway fee over limit as a protocol refusal. By the ADR the protocol does NOT refuse a base-under, ppm-over schedule, so OPS-21's parenthetical is false and no rule tells the wallet to apply the check, where, or with what class.
Fix: make FMI-19 a wallet-side check with a stated point (at selection and before the lnv2 receive/send call) and class (Retryable for receive per FMI-16, Permanent for send per FMI-17); correct OPS-21; amend the ADR-0029 note to cite FMI-19 as the resulting decision.
close_reason: Premise false (Opus; re-verified): the public SDK compares fee limits component-wise since v0.12.0 (commit d5febdf9d37, 2026-07-30, fedimint-lnv2-common gateway_api.rs is_within), applied on send and receive. OPS-21's '(the protocol refuses at the send)' is therefore true and SEC-7 is consistent with it; a wallet-side second enforcer would violate one-owner-per-rule. Only ADR-0029:26-29's lexicographic note is stale, and spec-y0b owns that amendment.

title: FMI-14 cites ADR-0030 §4 as owner of committed-route replay; ADR-0030/0022/0029/0003 need dated amendment notes; README:43 needs narrowing
description:
MAJOR (P1). Rewritten 2026-09-23 after the second four-model bead review; this text replaces the original (its README:43 claim was a misreading) and its round-1 correction (wrong about ADR-0029 and ADR-0003).

**What is real (verified).** README.md:43 says ADRs are "Canonical where they conflict with OLDER prose", so OPS-20/STO-33 (newer) already win over ADR-0030 §4 and no compliant implementation follows the ADR; the gap is that a reviewer cannot tell which is older without git, and that 02:181 (FMI-14) cites "ADR-0030 §4" as the OWNER of committed-route replay, which OPS-20 owns. docs/adr/0030:47-49: "after cache loss a send-required move's committed gateway is not recoverable from the op-log; such a re-drive resolves afresh" vs 03:416-421 (OPS-20): "the route MUST replay as recorded, from the cache and, after cache loss, from the gateway … the committed leg's metadata carries (STO-33)". docs/adr/0022:70-73 (backup must include in-flight move state) vs STO-28 / ADR-0025 (never the local stores) and FMI-32.

**What is NOT stale.** ADR-0029:26-29 says "Two facts about the SDK AT THE PINNED REVISION … `PaymentFee` compares lexicographically on base first". That is TRUE of the pin 72b1e5be (`send_fee.le(&PaymentFee::SEND_FEE_LIMIT)` over a derived `PartialOrd`, at send and at receive; the component-wise fix d5febdf9d37 is not an ancestor of the pin; it is in v0.12.0-beta.4+). It is stale only as a DECISION: FMI-19 now requires component-wise. ADR-0003:9's "federation IDs": ADR-0025:9 annotates its OWN text, not ADR-0003's; README:43 lets the newer SEC-24 win, so a one-line dated note on ADR-0003 is the cheap fix (do not argue it away).

**Fix.** (a) FMI-14: cite OPS-20 as the owner of committed-route replay; ADR-0030 §4 gets a dated amendment note "superseded by OPS-20/STO-33 (`gateway` / `send_gateway`), with OPS-20's legacy-metadata exception" (precedent: ADR-0004 "as amended", ADR-0028). (b) ADR-0022:70-73 → note pointing at ADR-0025/STO-28/SEC-24. (c) ADR-0029:26-29 → note: "true of the SDK before v0.12.0-beta.4 and of the pinned revision; the wallet's rule is FMI-19, which the pinned SDK does not enforce component-wise — a code-repository finding". (d) ADR-0003:9 → one-line note. title: Probe leg fee cap default is stated two incompatible ways (FMI-34 10 sats vs STO-13 max_fee 200 sats); STO-26's 'default-qualifying' is a misnamed retention category
description:
MAJOR (P1). Rewritten 2026-09-23 after the second four-model bead review; this text replaces the original ("three ways" — it is two) and its round-1 correction (which turned a default fix into a retention redesign).

**The defect (verified).** 02-fedimint-integration.md:461-462 (FMI-34): leg fee cap `max_fee` "(default 10 sats per leg in the standalone verb)". 05-persistence.md:257 (STO-13): seeded `max_fee 200_000` msat. 06:47-52 (ALC-3): "every planning and probing path MUST run under the stored Policy … its probe amount and leg fee cap (max_fee)". Two incompatible defaults for the same verb. Both are live in the reference implementation (wallet-cli's probe verb: "PER-LEG fee cap in millisatoshis (default 10000 = 10 sats)"; every daemon money verb: `policy.max_fee`).

**Not defects.** 05:470-471 (STO-26) "default-qualifying means `ok && amount_msat ≥ 20_000 && leg_fee_cap_msat ≤ 10_000`" is a RETENTION category with an explicit rule, misnamed, not a third default; its effect is limited to which attempts survive beyond seven days (STO-26 first keeps every attempt within 7 days plus the newest and newest-ok per source). ALC-27's leg-OUT `min(leg_cap, delivered_in − out_net)` (06:371-374) is not a contradiction: a stricter OUT cap satisfies a per-leg maximum.

**Fix.** FMI-34: delete "default 10 sats per leg in the standalone verb" and cite STO-13 (ALC-3 already makes the standalone probe run under the stored `max_fee`). STO-26: keep the category and its fixed constants, but NAME it accurately (it qualifies under the SEEDED defaults of STO-13: 20_000 / … — make the constants STO-13's seeded values by citation, or say the category is fixed and independent of later policy edits). Do NOT key pruning to the current or the at-write policy — that is a retention redesign and a separate decision; if wanted, it goes to chapter 11. Any standalone probe flag lands in API-44 (spec-ee9). A dedicated leg-cap Policy field is a separate product decision (not here; the former edge from spec-pe4 was dropped for that reason).

**Hand-off (done-condition 6):** the reference CLI's `probe` default changes from 10 to 200 sats per leg, which quadruples what ALC-26's `reservation(probe_amount, max_fee) = max(a + c, 2 × c)` reserves per probe; record it.

Owners: FMI-34, STO-26. Depends on nothing.
