title: ALC-28 step 2 decides on 'agent-created', a fact no row carries; OPS-42 must create the UserApproved row in the join's transaction and ALC-28 needs a repair transition table
description:
MAJOR (P1). Rewritten 2026-09-23 after the second four-model bead review; this text replaces the original (whose fix inferred provenance from a best-effort row) and its round-1 correction (which conflated approval, probe-gating and structural validity).

**The defect (verified).** 06-allocator-and-automation.md:399-402 (ALC-28 step 2): a joined federation whose row is Discovered/Rejected "and whose registry entry is agent-created" becomes AutoJoined/Passed; a joined federation with no row gets one "(source: Manual, AutoJoined, Passed)". 05:83 (STO-5): `FederationInfo {invite, db_prefix, joined_at}` — no actor, so "agent-created" is underivable. 03:605-609 (OPS-42): a user join "marks" a candidate UserApproved from a state that is neither AutoJoined nor UserApproved; it does not say a row is CREATED when none exists (06:390-391, ALC-37 implies it: "a user join writes it only when no AutoJoined row already exists"). 07:198-202 (SEC-16): a user's own join is the user's decision. Worse: DOM-3/ALC-37 probe-gate ANY joined federation without a UserApproved row, so if the row is not created the conformance environment's own A and B are probe-gated and CNF-13 refuses NotProbed — the set only works if the row exists.

**Fix — keep three facts distinct: user approval, probe-gated membership, structural validity.**
1. OPS-42: a user join writes its `UserApproved` candidate row `{source: Manual, structural: Passed, state: UserApproved}` in the SAME journal transaction as the registry row (exactly what FMI-31 already does for recovery: "in one journal transaction, write the registry row, terminalize the intent Done and write a UserApproved candidate"). Then "joined with no row" can only be an agent join or a legacy store, and the crash window disappears. DOM-12:100-101 ("by a user join from any state that is not already AutoJoined") gains "or from no row".
2. ALC-28 step 2: a repair TRANSITION TABLE, not a sentence — a joined federation whose row is absent → create `{source: Manual, structural: Passed, state: AutoJoined}` (fail-closed: probe-gated until `approve`, exactly ALC-37's rule for an unreadable row); a joined federation whose row is `Discovered` → `AutoJoined` (state only); a row whose `structural` is `Rejected(reason)` → do NOT rewrite it to `Passed` without re-checking (the round-1 text did; say what happens: leave structural as is, set state per the table, or re-run the structural check). Preserve `UserApproved`'s monotonicity; distinguish an absent row from an unreadable row. Do NOT infer "agent-created" from the `join:<fed>:<nonce>` ledger row (best-effort under OVR-4) and do not add an actor field; if provenance is ever needed it goes in `FederationInfo` under STO-30 with a legacy default that never silently becomes user approval.
3. Hand-off (done-condition 6): an existing store whose user joins predate the rule has no candidate rows; after the change those federations are probe-gated until `approve`. A silent backfill of `UserApproved` would be "fabricating acceptance" — name the migration decision (one-time backfill vs operator `approve`) for the code repository; do not decide it here.

FederationInfo's field types are spec-tj5's. Owners: OPS-42 (creation, transaction), ALC-28 (the repair table), DOM-12 (the transition sentence). Scenario: a user join with a crash after the registry write is impossible (one transaction); a legacy joined federation with no row is probe-gated, then `approve` releases it.

Depends on nothing. spec-60q depends on this one (its counters count agent joins under these rules).

title: Unaffordable route hint: CONTEXT.md re-resolves it, FMI-14 step 2 / OPS-22 terminalize Permanent
description:
MAJOR, Fable, verified. CONTEXT.md:197-207 (Route hint): kept only while it holds, otherwise re-resolved under the same fee cap ... so a holding hint can still prove unaffordable and be re-resolved. 02-fedimint-integration.md:186 (FMI-14 step 2): the action's route hint, if it still holds (FMI-13) — taken; step 3's cheapest fitting candidate is reached only when the hint does not hold. 03:507-511 (OPS-22): receive-leg cap check ... over is persisted first, then Retryable for Evacuate, Permanent otherwise. A funding Move with a holding hint whose quote rose over the cap is Permanent; the same move without a hint is Retryable and re-priced (FMI-14 step 3, 02:188-191). Different terminals for the same economic state, observable on the ledger; the glossary owns behaviour nothing states.
Fix: add to FMI-14 step 2: a holding hint whose receive quote at the amount exceeds the cap is discarded and step 3 runs; or delete the glossary clause and let OPS-22's Permanent stand. CONTEXT.md cites the owner.

## Review corrections (2026-09-23, four-model bead review: Fable, Opus, Astra, Sol)
CONFIRMED by all four (Opus: borderline minor — only the glossary disagrees; the requirements are consistent with each other). Take option A (Fable, Sol: 'a hint, never a constraint' is the stronger existing decision): FMI-14 step 2 says a holding hint whose route proves unaffordable at the amount is discarded and step 3 runs; OPS-22 terminalizes only after that resolution fails. Correction (Astra): checking the destination receive quote alone is insufficient — a hint can pass it and fail the combined send/receive check or size to nothing; define the fallback for the complete UNCOMMITTED hinted route after pricing/sizing, and keep OPS-20/FMI-23's committed-route rules untouched. Only allocator funding Moves carry a hint (API-18/API-31 put no gateway on the wire; probe legs carry none) — worth saying. Absorb DEF-5 (09:49, 'the whole candidate set, never by a candidate's position') here: replace its duplicate selection rule with citations that preserve the hint and bounded-scan exceptions. CONTEXT.md Route hint cites FMI-14.

## Second review (2026-09-23, four-model bead review round 2: Fable, Opus, Astra, Sol)
CONFIRMED (P1 kept: FMI-14 step 2's 'holds' IS the glossary's definition, so two readings are both normative and produce different terminals; Opus's P2 reading — 'the requirements agree, only CONTEXT.md disagrees' — is noted). One sentence of the round-1 correction is WRONG: 'Only allocator funding Moves carry a hint' — ALC-17 stamps 'gateway: route hint' on every Evacuate too (06: 'Evacuate {fee_cap: components.at(amount), gateway: route hint, fee_cap_components}'); for an Evacuate the receive-leg over-cap is already Retryable (OPS-22), so the behavioural change is for Move only, but the fallback must be written for both kinds and their sizing. 'OPS-22 terminalizes only after that resolution fails' must not turn exhausted selection into a Permanent where FMI-14 prescribes retryable exhaustion. FMI-14 owns hint acceptance and fallback; OPS-20 preserves committed routes; DEF-5:49's duplicate selection rule becomes a citation. spec-bqv lands after this.

title: Policy validity predicate is two lines (ALC-7, ALC-20); DOM-15 / API-20 require rejecting any invalid policy naming the field
description:
MAJOR, Fable + Astra + Sol. 01-domain-model.md:120-123 (DOM-15): MUST validate the stored row, MUST refuse to run under an invalid one, MUST reject an edit that would store one (API-20); 04-api-contract.md:289-290 (API-20): 422 policy_invalid naming the field. Owners of validity: 06:126-127 (ALC-7) max_fee_bps_of_move 0 or above 10 000; 06:294-295 (ALC-20) a bps above 10 000 or the pair (0, 0). Nothing else: min_interval_secs > base_interval_secs makes ALC-38's at most the base / at least the minimum (06:566) and ALC-39's clamp (06:608) undefined; probe_min_successes = 0, spending_target > per_fed_cap, probe_ttl_secs > 604 800 (silently ineffective under STO-26's constant window) are all accepted. Two implementations accept different PUT /v1/policy bodies; CNF-33 / CNF-26 cannot decide it.

## Review corrections (2026-09-23, four-model bead review: Fable, Opus, Astra, Sol)
CONFIRMED by all four; not self-contained. Owner: ALC-54 (next free ALC) holds the exhaustive predicate; ALC-7 and ALC-20 keep owning their two ranges and are cited; DOM-15, API-20, HST-6/STO-13's start-time validation and the standalone overrides (ALC-3) all reference ALC-54. Verified undefined: min_interval_secs > base_interval_secs (ALC-39's clamp; Rust's Ord::clamp panics); ALC-52's max(min_successes - 1, 1) at 0 unless saturating; base_interval_secs = 0 (busy loop); probe_amount < 5 000 msat (can never mint, FMI-16); discover_pass_deadline_secs = 0. The other examples are DECISIONS, not automatically invalid (Astra, Sol): spending_target > per_fed_cap, probe_min_successes = 0, probe_ttl_secs > 604 800 (ALC-25 explicitly reads 'the retained history, which STO-26 prunes') may be legal-but-ineffective — the predicate must say which, and end with 'all other correctly typed values are legal'. Deterministic first-error ordering for the named field; decoding errors distinct from semantic invalidity. Upgrade hazard (Opus): DOM-15/STO-13 make a resident host refuse to start on an invalid stored row, so tightening the predicate can brick an existing store — choose a disposition (refuse naming the field, or grandfather + warn) and add the code-repo hand-off. Depends on spec-9iq if it adds a policy field.

## Second review (2026-09-23, four-model bead review round 2: Fable, Opus, Astra, Sol)
CONFIRMED; ALC-54 is the next free ALC (ALC-50 withdrawn; verify). Corrections: several round-1 'verified undefined' examples are not established — probe_amount < 5 000 is not automatically invalid (the probe is a grossed-up move; the minimum binds its incoming contract, not the requested net); max(min_successes − 1, 1) at zero needs a stated arithmetic domain, not an unsigned-underflow argument; zero intervals/deadlines may be invalid OR disabling, and the choice must be stated. 'Grandfather + warn' conflicts with DOM-15's command to refuse an invalid stored policy unless DOM-15 is amended — say which. ALC-54 states the treatment of every correctly typed value, deterministic error ordering, stored-policy validation and upgrade behaviour; API-27:368-370's parse-time subset ('--max-fee-bps-of-move 1..=10000, --evac-fee-bps 0..=10000 at parse time') must be stated as exactly those, or extended, or two CLIs diverge on which invalid policies never reach PUT. The edge to spec-9iq was removed (no policy field is added there).

title: ALC-17's Unhealthy evacuation branch is unreachable: the snapshot only holds federations whose light probe succeeded
description:
MAJOR, Sol, verified. 06-allocator-and-automation.md:29-32 (ALC-1): the snapshot carries the joined, open federations whose light probe succeeded (FMI-25) ... its healthy flag — FMI-25's quorum_live, the threshold read that succeeded. 02-fedimint-integration.md:395-397 (FMI-25): a federation whose light probe errors is dropped from the snapshot with a warning and is therefore neither scored nor evacuated that cycle. 06:260-261 (ALC-17): Unhealthy when it is not healthy. healthy is always true for a snapshot member, so the branch has no constructible input and CONTEXT.md:80-88's backstop for unplanned degradation is not delivered.
Fix: keep a bounded negative liveness verdict in the snapshot (a threshold read that answered below quorum, distinct from an indeterminate transport error), or remove Unhealthy from ALC-17 and the glossary's claim.

## Review corrections (2026-09-23, four-model bead review: Fable, Opus, Astra, Sol)

Option 1 is flawed (Fable, Opus, Astra): a federation whose threshold read fails or answers below quorum cannot sign the lnv2 send an evacuation needs, so a negative-liveness Evacuate would be Retryable forever; and 'a threshold read that answered below quorum' is not a usable observation (a successful threshold read has reached its threshold). Complete the cleanup: remove the snapshot's healthy flag from ALC-1 (an unused input of a pure function under OVR-6), keep the Unhealthy ReasonCode vocabulary, fix ALC-48's sentence and CONTEXT.md:87-88 AND :95-96 ('secondarily by probes detecting degradation'). title: OPS-11 / ALC-53 use 'world generation', 'plan authority', 'balance authority' and 'balance facts', none defined: replace with the owned counters and state the in-batch rule
description:
MAJOR (P1). Rewritten 2026-09-23 after the second four-model bead review; this text replaces the original (which proposed DEFINING the three terms — do not) and its round-1 correction.

**The defect (verified).** 03-operation-lifecycle.md:167-169 (OPS-11): the batch MUST be refused whole on "a stale policy generation (ALC-41), a changed world generation, an invalid plan or balance-facts authority, or more than one occurrence". 06-allocator-and-automation.md:773-775 (ALC-53): "the world generation, the plan authority, the balance authority". CONTEXT.md:325-330 (Generation) defines exactly three counters — a balance generation per federation (OPS-13), a membership generation (OPS-6), a policy generation (ALC-41). Nothing defines issuance, content, invalidation or equivalence of "world generation", "plan authority", "balance authority" or "balance facts", so whole-batch acceptance cannot be implemented or reviewed independently.

**Fix — replace, don't define; no lease/token machinery (fails the refactor test).** OPS-11 enumerates the observable comparisons whose change rejects the batch whole, by CITATION to the owners (OPS-13's third bullet already states the balance-generation rule; OPS-6 already says every admission advances the membership generation "so that no allocator plan computed over the world before this admission can commit"; ALC-35: a plan is "valid only with the balance generation that authorized it"; ALC-41 the policy generation; OPS-41's fence: no plan or balance facts issued during a raw terminal write or membership change). Then state, in OPS-11, the two things implementations will otherwise do differently:
1. **What a "balance fact" is** — the sampled spendable balance per federation that the plan was computed over (FMI-27) — and that ALC-53 item 2 compares it by the federation's balance generation, not by value.
2. **Self-advance within a batch.** OPS-6 advances the balance generation of every federation the action touches and the membership generation on EVERY successful admission, including each decision the batch itself admits; unless the batch is exempt from its own advances, the second decision of any batch fails ALC-53 item 2. State the rule (recommended: the batch's comparisons are evaluated once, before its first admission, under one fence; the batch's own admissions do not invalidate its remaining decisions; any OTHER admission or a registry write in between rejects the rest of the batch whole).
Also: FMI-8 "A join MUST invalidate any allocator plan computed over the world before it (ALC-32)" — ALC-32 defines no invalidation, and OPS-6's membership generation is advanced by admission, not by the registry write that actually changes membership; make the join/open/recovery commit advance the membership generation (owner OPS-6 or OPS-42) so the race is closed.

ALC-53, ALC-34 (06:530-531), ALC-38 step 9 and the glossary cite OPS-11; ALC-38 step 5's "authorize planning" is the OPS-41 fence, not one of these. Decide OPS-39's `conflict — an admission racing a membership change (OPS-41)` row (a fresh-admission guard or plan invalidation only) and make owner and mapping agree; spec-euo edits the neighbouring OPS-39/API-15 rows, so land this first.

**Scenario:** a batch of two decisions; (a) a join commits between plan and commit → the whole batch is refused; (b) a user pay is admitted between the batch's first and second decision → state which of "whole batch refused" and "one decision dropped" applies, per the rule chosen in 2.

Owners: OPS-11; OPS-6 for the join advance. Depends on nothing.

title: Journal key: STO-1 prefixes every key with 0x00, STO-5 says [tag] ++ id_bytes, STO-18 requires an exactly nine-byte ledger tail
description:
MAJOR, Sol, verified. 05-persistence.md:16-18 (STO-1): inside journal.db every journal key is prefixed 0x00, and a key outside that prefix is not part of the journal. 05:55 (STO-5): every journal key is [tag] ++ id_bytes, the ledger key 0x05 ++ be64(seq). 05:388-395 (STO-18): the tail is the lexicographically greatest 0x05 key, which MUST be a canonical nine-byte key; a tail key that is not exactly nine bytes is the fence. Either 0x00 is an outer namespace the nine bytes sit under (then STO-5's key is the logical key and the raw key is ten bytes, and every scan/prefix rule must say which), or the ledger key is nine bytes and STO-1 is wrong. Two implementations write mutually unreadable stores.
Fix: state the raw byte sequence once in STO-5 (e.g. 0x00 ++ tag ++ id_bytes, with lengths), distinguish namespace prefix from logical key wherever a length or lexicographic rule appears (STO-18, STO-10 index keys), and correct the nine-byte sentences.

## Review corrections (2026-09-23, four-model bead review: Fable, Opus, Astra, Sol)
CONFIRMED by all four (severity split: Opus minor, Fable/Astra major, Sol blocker). Reconcilable reading (Opus, Astra): STO-1's 0x00 is a namespace ('a key outside that prefix is not part of the journal'; STO-3 uses the same pattern for client.db, and the withdrawn DEF-24 / CNF-51 read it so), STO-5's [tag] ++ id_bytes is the LOGICAL key within it, and the raw key is 0x00 ++ logical. The defect is that 'journal key' names both, so STO-18's 'not exactly nine bytes' is literally false of raw bytes. Fix, one sentence in STO-5: keys and lengths in this chapter are logical keys under STO-1's 0x00 namespace; the raw ledger key is 00 || 05 || be64(seq), ten bytes; then check every scan, index and canonical-length statement (STO-1/10/18/19/20/22/24/25) says which view it means. Do NOT change any byte or replace nine with ten (OVR-14). The raw-byte truth is a fact about existing stores, not a choice — if any doubt remains, the code repository's persistence layer is the input.

## Second review (2026-09-23, four-model bead review round 2: Fable, Opus, Astra, Sol)
CONFIRMED; the reference store settles the reading (wallet-fedimint/src/journal.rs: 'All journal rows live under the app prefix [0x00] (db.with_prefix(vec![0x00]))', APP_PREFIX = 0x00): journal rows carry logical keys [tag] ++ id_bytes under the 0x00 app prefix, so the raw ledger key is 00 || 05 || be64(seq), ten bytes, and STO-5/STO-18's 'nine bytes' are logical. Scope the sentence 'lengths in this chapter are logical' to journal.db: in client.db STO-3's '[0x01] ++ u32_le(db_prefix), exactly five bytes' IS raw (the 0x01 is the tag). STO-5 owns the physical/logical distinction; STO-1/STO-18 cite. While checking the index statements, decide the nit STO-25:461 'all five 0x04 status keys' vs STO-10 'Done is never indexed' (checking all five for absence may be intentional — say so or fix the count). P2 defensible; P1 kept until the sentence lands.

title: 'Serves' is defined in CONTEXT.md as including 'performs', but FMI-11 / FMI-13 use it for a decoded RoutingInfo before any operation
description:
MAJOR, Sol, verified. CONTEXT.md:143-153 (Serves): a gateway serves when it is on the vetted list, validates, an economically viable amount can be sized over it, AND it performs — completes every leg it quoted. 02-fedimint-integration.md:131 (FMI-11): a decoded RoutingInfo means the gateway serves that federation; FMI-13 (02:166-173) uses serves before sizing or performance; ALC eligibility (06:235-245) asks whether a gateway serves. title: CLI argument grammar is absent: HST-10 ends its flag list in '…', API-25 enumerates verb names only, so CNF-26 cannot be judged
description:
MAJOR, Opus. 08-hosts-and-deployment.md:175-181 (HST-10): the standalone-only verb shapes and flags are the set API-25 enumerates ... (--per-fed-cap, --evac-fee-*, --occurrence, …). 04-api-contract.md:341-354 (API-25 / API-26): verb names and the request fields each sends, not positional vs flag arguments, not the arguments of probe, discover, tick, status, history --fed, show <seq>, not the complete override list. 06:50 (ALC-3): HST-10 lists the flags. 10:313-335 (CNF-26) asserts each verb sends exactly the named fields; without the grammar two compliant CLIs are script-incompatible and the scenario cannot be staged uniformly.
Fix: one API-n table: every verb's positional arguments, flags, defaults and mode (client / standalone / both), including the full override flag list; HST-10 and ALC-3 cite it.

## Review corrections (2026-09-23, four-model bead review: Fable, Opus, Astra, Sol)
CONFIRMED by all four. Corrections: the grammar is INCOMPLETE, not absent — API-27 (policy flags), API-38 (<key> --timeout), API-39 (approve <hex>, show <key>), API-40 (history filters), API-41 (--nonce/--occurrence/--fee-cap/--to/--fed, 'move --occurrence defaults to 0') and API-25's global flags exist; the new table (API-44, next free API) must absorb them by citation, never copy a default into a second normative table. Genuinely unspecified: positional vs flag arguments and shapes for pay, move, receive, direct-inflow, join, recover, probe, discover, tick, status, history --fed, show <seq>; repeatability; mutually exclusive pairs; client/standalone availability; the full override list and which Policy fields standalone tick/status may override (ALC-3, OPS-7 'MUST be validated'). The grammar is not derivable from this repository (Fable, Opus): name the input — ratify the code repository's CLI --help — so the agent does not invent one that gives the existing CLI a finding per divergence. HST-10 and ALC-3 cite API-44. Depends on spec-6w6 (adds config/flags) and the new default-fee_cap bead (the grammar states defaults it cannot invent); land after spec-9iq if it adds a probe flag.

## Second review (2026-09-23, four-model bead review round 2: Fable, Opus, Astra, Sol)
CONFIRMED (incomplete, not absent — API-27, API-38-41 exist; 08:175-181 ends in '…'). API-44 is the next free API (verify). Ratify the reference CLI's --help (money verbs flag-only: --from, --to, --amount, …; join/recover take a positional invite) rather than invent. The grammar must carry: the fee_cap default (spec-w0c), the discovery flags (spec-6w6), and the older-attempt reclaim selector spec-cuw decides — new edge to spec-cuw. spec-pe4's validity predicate determines which invalid values the CLI refuses at parse time (API-27:368-370 range-checks two flags 'at parse time'); coordinate, no edge.

title: OPS-5's '24 hours when no perform timeout is configured' is unreachable under HST-2's 600 s default
description:
MAJOR, Fable + Opus, verified. 03-operation-lifecycle.md:72-74 (OPS-5): probe legs are each awaited to terminal under the host's perform timeout ... or 24 hours when none is configured. 08-hosts-and-deployment.md:32 (HST-2): WALLETD_PERFORM_TIMEOUT_SECS unset or empty -> 600 s, 0 disables it; 08:159-160 (HST-9) standalone the same. None configured is 600 s, so the 24-hour bound is unreachable unless none means 0 — in which case a disabled timeout is not disabled for probe legs. Undecidable as written.
Fix: replace with: or 24 hours when the timeout is disabled (0); or delete the clause.

## Review corrections (2026-09-23, four-model bead review: Fable, Opus, Astra, Sol)
DOWNGRADED to minor (Fable, Opus, Astra; Sol keeps major). Reconcilable reading: 'none is configured' = the resolved perform deadline is disabled (0). The clause is reachable only with 0 set and only for probe legs. Fix, one line in OPS-5: 'or 24 hours when the resolved perform timeout is disabled (0)'; HST-2 and HST-9 quote it. Do not delete the fallback as if it were an editorial equivalent (Astra: that changes behaviour).

## Second review (2026-09-23, four-model bead review round 2: Fable, Opus, Astra, Sol)
CONFIRMED, P2. Cite OPS-5 from HST-2/HST-9 rather than quote it (one owner).

title: Egress policy (FMI-40) covers gateway requests only; meta_override_url and discovery config fetches inherit nothing
description:
MAJOR, Astra, PLAUSIBLE. 02-fedimint-integration.md:138 (FMI-40): the wallet MUST NOT let a guardian direct its egress — but the address, redirect and DNS checks apply before any gateway request. 02:402 (FMI-26) reads an explicitly untrusted meta_override_url; 02:440 (FMI-28) fetches candidate configurations supplied by discovery. Neither path inherits the gateway restrictions, so a malicious guardian or poisoned feed (07:23) can induce requests to link-local / private addresses; rejecting the fetched metadata happens after connecting.
Fix: one egress rule for every untrusted endpoint the wallet contacts (gateways, override metadata, discovery sources, candidate config fetches), with explicit exceptions (the operator's own Observer base) and the redirect / DNS-rebinding rules; conformance cases per path.

## Review corrections (2026-09-23, four-model bead review: Fable, Opus, Astra, Sol)
CONFIRMED by all four; scope corrected. Strong half: the meta_override_url fetch (FMI-26) is an HTTP GET to a guardian-chosen URL — a real SSRF vector (blind: the wallet parses and never returns the body). Weak half: the discovery preview (FMI-28/ALC-28) speaks the federation transport (FMI-36: iroh, WebSocket, HTTP) to the invite's endpoints; an iroh endpoint has no host to check, and applying the gateway HTTP rules indiscriminately would break FMI-36. Extending egress to guardian endpoints also refuses every loopback conformance federation (CNF-17/CNF-20's announced C included) unless the private-network allowance (spec-iq9, now folded here) covers that class. Fix: one owner for untrusted-endpoint egress (extend FMI-40 or a new SEC-26), cited by FMI-26, FMI-28, FMI-40 and the host rules, deciding: operator-configured bases (the Observer {base}, once spec-6w6 gives it a home) vs URLs supplied by guardians or feeds; user-supplied join/recover invites are exempt (the user's decision, SEC-16); redirects, address changes at connect time, DNS rebinding; proxy behaviour under HST-2; transport-specific enforcement; which private-network exceptions apply per class, never the link-local/metadata range. Simpler product option for the meta path (Opus): stop reading the override-served expiry, which 'never schedules on its own' anyway. Conformance cases per path. Depends on spec-6w6.

## Second review (2026-09-23, four-model bead review round 2: Fable, Opus, Astra, Sol)
CONFIRMED as corrected. Decisions to take IN THE EDIT, not to leave open: (1) owner is FMI-40 (it already is the egress rule and SEC-17 points at it; a new SEC-26 would be a second owner). (2) FMI-40 requires 'the address actually connected to MUST be one the rule approved', while HST-2 routes gateway routing_info (FMI-11) and the Observer (FMI-28) through an operator's HTTP(S)_PROXY via CONNECT, where the wallet never learns the connected address — resolve it (the rule applies to the resolved destination before CONNECT; the proxy is inside SEC-3's trust boundary). (3) The meta_override_url GET is performed by the client SDK's meta service, not by wallet code; the only egress rule implementable above the presupposed SDK for that path is 'do not read the override-served expiry' (a behaviour change, say so) or the wallet fetches the merged meta itself — pick one. (4) A poisoned discovery feed can hand the wallet an invite whose WebSocket guardian endpoints are link-local; for WebSocket/HTTP endpoints from a feed this is the STRONGER half (iroh endpoints have no host and stay out). (5) An exemption for user-supplied invites is a decision, not an inference from SEC-16; the conformance environment does not require loopback federations, so any restriction needs explicit test allowances. Cite slip: the poisoned-feed threat is 07:29-31, not 07:23. spec-iq9 is CLOSED into this bead: FMI-40's 'A host MAY offer an explicit configuration that permits private-network gateways' is a MAY no compliant host can exercise under HST-2/HST-3's closed surfaces — either file the chapter-11 entry for the allowance (and mark the MAY as governed by it) or strike the MAY; do it here. Edge to spec-6w6 kept (the operator-configured Observer base is one of the classes).

title: Vetted-list reads and sequential peer /status reads have no per-request or per-cycle bound; a silent guardian stalls the cycle
description:
MAJOR, Sol, PLAUSIBLE. 02-fedimint-integration.md:112-121 (vetted list reads), 02:416-419 (peer /status reads for corroboration) and the boundary table 02:282-298 (FMI-22), which omits both. 06:561-605 (the scheduler cycle, ALC-38 / ALC-48): a non-answering guardian can therefore stall the cycle, readiness and evacuation indefinitely.
Fix: add rows to FMI-22: connect / total bounds per read, an aggregate per federation and per cycle, cancellation behaviour, and the resulting classification (no signal vs failure) for the light probe and the shutdown corroboration.

## Review corrections (2026-09-23, four-model bead review: Fable, Opus, Astra, Sol)
CONFIRMED by all four; understated: FMI-25's session_count threshold read is equally unbounded (FMI-38 bounds only waits 'while driving an intent'), and ALC-40 runs 'after every cycle' so it cannot rescue a cycle stuck before completion; HST-6 excludes status dry runs from the perform timeout. Fix: rows in FMI-22 for the per-guardian vetted-list read (FMI-10), the per-peer /status read (FMI-26), the threshold read (FMI-25) and the override-metadata fetch, plus a per-federation and per-cycle light-probe budget; the numbers are a design value the agent chooses (suggest mirroring FMI-11's 5 s connect / 10 s total per guardian); cancellation semantics; and the classification of a timeout — a timed-out guardian 'lists nothing' (FMI-10), a timed-out peer is 'no signal' (FMI-26; a timeout must never manufacture corroboration), a timed-out threshold read is a light-probe error dropped per FMI-25/ALC-48. ALC-38 cites the aggregate-cycle guarantee.

## Second review (2026-09-23, four-model bead review round 2: Fable, Opus, Astra, Sol)
CONFIRMED. Add the observable consequence that makes it P1: ALC-45 publishes readiness only when a cycle ends ('A cycle that plans, commits and then completes … MUST publish automation_blocked: None'), so a cycle stuck in a light-probe read leaves the PREVIOUS cycle's automation_ready: true on /v1/health indefinitely. The fix either bounds the cycle (the per-cycle budget) or requires readiness to go not-ready when a cycle overruns. Scenario here: a guardian that never answers its vetted-list read does not stall the cycle and readiness reflects it. The timeouts are engineering values (ADR-0032), not chapter-11 material.

title: Three scenario assertions contradict their owners: CNF-15 timestamps by seq, CNF-16 'records nothing', CNF-14 one-tick drain
description:
MAJOR (P1). Rewritten 2026-09-23 after the second four-model bead review; this text replaces the original (whose title and first paragraph still described the pre-split coverage bead — the coverage work is spec-tc0 and its (ii)-(iv) siblings).

Scope: exactly three scenario assertions that contradict the requirement they demonstrate. Verified at 4ea6c02.

1. **CNF-15** (10:284-285) asserts "timestamps non-decreasing by `seq`". DOM-11 (01:87-89): timestamps "carry no ordering authority"; STO-16 (05:362-363): "A fresh intent-backed row takes `created_at_ms` from `Intent.created_at_ms` (not the clock)" — a retry row keeps the original `created_at_ms`. False even for `updated_at_ms` within CNF-15's own session (a lower-seq row terminalizes later). Fix: narrow to what is observable (`seq` is the order) or delete the clause.
2. **CNF-16** (10:194-195) asserts a preflight failure "is a no-attempt that records nothing". ALC-27 (06:361-367): "begin a session (STO-26); write the umbrella `probe:<fed>:<nonce>` row (STO-6); … preflight". Fix: say "records no attempt and changes no verdict", and take the umbrella row's terminal status and the session cleanup from spec-xm8 (this is a real dependency — the round-1 text's "independent of every other fix" was wrong).
3. **CNF-14** (10:113-120) demands that after "a tick runs" A is drained to "below OPS-44's sizing floor" in ONE tick, while ADR-0029:93-95 expressly allows "the source drains in several operations" and the fixture fixes neither fees nor viability. With the environment's cap room above the balance and the default (200 sat, 300 bps) cap one `largest_fitting` pass does drain it at ordinary fees, so this is fixture precision, not a contradiction: fix the fixture (a route that drains in one operation, fees stated) or assert progress over occurrences. Review CNF-20's drain fixture alongside. Use spec-1nc's credit vocabulary wherever a monetary equality is asserted.

Owner for each: the scenario, citing the requirement it demonstrates. Depends on spec-xm8 (item 2).

title: FMI-41 / API-42 call a funded contract 'not claimable' when expired: funding expiry and claimability conflated; no SDK retries a claim
description:
BLOCKER (P0; promoted in the second review: an implementation that follows FMI-41 literally answers `not_claimable` for a funded, claimable contract, which leaves funds unreachable by any described path — funds lost). Rewritten 2026-09-23; this text replaces the original.

**Protocol facts — verified at the pin 72b1e5be and at upstream master (57c7e8c57c5); do not re-derive from the beads.**
1. The lnv2 server checks `expiration_or_fee` only when an incoming contract is FUNDED (`process_output` → `ContractExpired`). Claiming an existing incoming contract (`process_input`, `LightningInputV0::Incoming`: remove the contract, verify the aggregated decryption key, decrypt the preimage, pay `claim_pk` else `refund_pk`) applies NO time check. A funded incoming contract has no claim deadline; it is claimable until consumed.
2. The client's `Expired` comes from the server's `await_incoming_contract`, which returns `None` only when, in one transaction, no funded contract exists and expiry has passed — after which funding is rejected. So an `Expired` receive was NEVER funded: nothing exists to re-claim, and API-42's `Expired` arm can only ever answer `not_claimable`. The round-1 sentence "Stranded-via-Expired … is still claimable" was wrong.
3. No SDK version retries a rejected claim. The receive state machine submits the claim once; when the mint outputs never confirm it reports `ReceiveOperationState::Failure`. At the pin a claim the client cannot build PANICS the executor (`receive_sm.rs:134` `expect("Cannot claim input, additional funding needed")`); on master only (f675cd3ad02, 2026-08-10, in no tag) that became `FinalReceiveOperationState::Uneconomical`, a terminal OPS-16's map does not know. There is no public re-claim entry point in the lnv2 client; the claim material (claim keypair, aggregated decryption key) lives in the client store's state-machine record.

**The defects in the set (verified).** 02-fedimint-integration.md:328-335 (FMI-41): a rejected claim "MUST be retried until the contract's expiry has passed" (no referent: a funded contract has no claim expiry; and no SDK retries) and the explicit re-claim reports "not claimable" when the contract "is expired or already consumed" (conflates funding expiry with claimability). 02:320 (FMI-37 receive row): "the claim transaction was rejected and the retries FMI-41 requires are exhausted" describes a mechanism that does not exist. 04-api-contract.md:580-584 (API-42): `{key}` MUST name an operation whose incoming contract reached "a terminal non-claim (Expired or Failed)". The useful re-claim case is exactly receive `Failure` (claim rejected, contract funded and unconsumed) — it IS reachable; only the "expired → not claimable" clause makes it useless. Conflicts with CONTEXT.md:296 "A delayed app open does NOT forfeit an already-settled payment".

**Fix (unconditional — the chapter-11 branch of the original is dead).**
- FMI-41: state the recovery state — receive `Failure` after a funded contract ⇒ the contract is funded and claimable indefinitely until consumed; drop the retry-until-expiry clause; bound the automatic retry by count or backoff (or state that there is none and re-claim is the recovery); distinguish a transient re-claim failure from the definitive `not_claimable` (contract consumed, or never funded); replay after a lost response; durable evidence sufficient to answer `claimed` even if the best-effort reclaim ledger row was lost; preserve the original failed/stranded evidence.
- FMI-37's receive row re-derived from the above. OPS-16's map: word it as "any other final state → `Failed` with the detail" so `Uneconomical` cannot fall outside it; add a prohibition (FMI-16 or the DEF-16 family) that an incoming contract whose claim the wallet cannot fund MUST end in a state, never stop the client (the pin's panic is a DEF-16-class freeze; FMI-16's `amount − gw_quote ≥ 5 000` pre-check does not bound the federation's claim fee).
- API-42: precondition names `Failed`; keep the `Expired` arm only as a documented `not_claimable`. Addressing of older attempts is spec-cuw's.
- Scenario, a REACHABLE fixture: a contract funded before expiry, an unsuccessful claim leaving it unconsumed, then a successful explicit re-claim AFTER the funding expiry → `claimed`, balance rises once, the original failure evidence kept. (Not "the gateway funded late" — that cannot happen.)
- Hand-off (done-condition 6): the pinned SDK exposes no re-claim and no claim retry (the fork patch eaa35c03067 "retry rejected claims and reclaim parked receives" is on a branch outside the pin); the wallet must re-submit the claim input with the operation's stored claim material, which needs an SDK entry point or a read of the client module's records. Record in the code repository's open findings; ADR-0032 already makes fork patches requirements, so this is not a reason to soften FMI-41.

Owners: FMI-41, FMI-37, API-42, OPS-16, OPS-27; HST-32 cites. spec-cuw depends on this bead.

title: 'trusted' move record (STO-11 validity table) and 'probed' federation (three senses) are used normatively and defined nowhere
description:
MAJOR (P1). Rewritten 2026-09-23 after the second four-model bead review; this text replaces the original (its "trusted" predicate rejected valid direct inflows and its "probed" fix forced two facts into one word).

**(1) "trusted" move record — used normatively, defined nowhere (verified).** 03-operation-lifecycle.md:145-147 (OPS-9) "The allocator projection weakens by move-record phase when the record is trusted"; 03:263 (OPS-45) skips pre-fund admission "when the cached move record is trusted"; 03:633 (OPS-30) "pristine (phase Created, trusted, …)"; 06:541-542 (ALC-35) "A corrupt move record falls back to the strict projection". CONTEXT.md has no entry; 05:209-239 (STO-11) has no trust rule; ADR-0024:41-43 lists "Missing, corrupt, mismatched, oversized, or impossible" but no requirement does. Trust releases reservations (Sending drops the outbound) and skips admission, so the predicate changes money admission and /v1/status.

Fix: STO-11 owns VALIDITY of a record, as a table conditional on the action and phase, from locally checkable correspondence: decodes; key equals the row key; `to`/`from`/`send_required` equal the action's (STO-11 already fixes `send_required = false` and `from = None` for a receive-only DirectInflow — so a `Settled` DirectInflow legitimately has NO `send_op`; the predicate MUST NOT require one); amount and cap transformations permitted per action; current-attempt correspondence (a record from another attempt is stale, not trusted); artifacts required vs optional per phase (Sending/Settled/Stranded need `send_op` only when `send_required`; Invoiced needs `invoice` + `recv_op`); the treatment of missing, malformed, stale and contradictory records (fallback to the strict projection). OPS-9 owns the resulting PROJECTION; OPS-30 and ALC-35 cite; OPS-45 stops using the word once spec-dgj lands (its rewrite keys on reassembled artifacts). Scenario: a valid settled direct inflow (no send_op) is trusted; a cross-attempt record is not.

**(2) "probed" federation — three senses (verified).** 06:31 (ALC-1) "whether it is probed"; 06:93 (ALC-5) "not eligible to fund, or not probed (ALC-15)" — ALC-15's `probe_gate_ok`; 06:491 (ALC-32 step 5) "exceeds the number of probed federations" and 06:615 (ALC-39) "per probed federation" — the LIGHT-probed snapshot members (every snapshot member passed the light probe); 03:476 "probed in order" is the bisection, unrelated. A successful light probe, an active-probe `Passed` verdict (ALC-25) and user approval (ALC-37) are different facts.

Fix: ALC-1 names the snapshot field by its exact predicate (ALC-37's `probe_gate_ok`, from ALC-25/ALC-37) and ALC-5 uses it verbatim; ALC-32 step 5 and ALC-39 say "snapshot federations" (a count of light-probed members is meaningful on its own — keep it as that, do not force it into `probe_gate_ok`). Never substitute route validation for active-probe qualification. Both: CONTEXT.md gains the terms citing their owners.

Owners: STO-11, OPS-9; ALC-1, ALC-5, ALC-32, ALC-39. Depends on spec-dgj (its rewrite removes one "trusted" use) and spec-j8w (which rewrites the ALC-39 sentence). Split into two beads if picked up by two agents; one agent can do both.

title: Untyped persisted fields: WatchState (STO-12), EvacuationSupersessionRecord (STO-25), FederationInfo (STO-5) break upgrade-in-place
description:
MAJOR, promoted from the minors (Opus, Astra, Sol; Fable keeps it minor). 05-persistence.md:241-242 (STO-12) WatchState fields carry no types: discover_backlog (bool? a count?), discover_rotation, last_discover_ms; 05:458-459 (STO-25) the sidecar fields old_attempt, refusal, old_cap_components?, … carry no types or domains; 05:83 (STO-5) FederationInfo {invite, db_prefix, joined_at (seconds)} gives no field types, and the InviteCode encoding is unstated because STO-5 says the string form appears 'only in CandidateRecord.invite' (FMI-20 contemplates an invite that does not parse). These are on-disk JSON under OVR-14's upgrade-in-place contract: two implementations can write bool against u8, or an id array against hex, and cannot read each other's stores. Fix: give every field a type, domain, optionality and STO-30 default, as STO-9, STO-15 and STO-26 do; do not claim types that are inferable elsewhere are unknown — complete the tables. Owners: STO-5, STO-12, STO-25, STO-30. (spec-nwm no longer owns FederationInfo's typing.)

## Second review (2026-09-23, four-model bead review round 2: Fable, Opus, Astra, Sol)
CONFIRMED and UNDERSTATED — new LEAD item (Fable, verified in the reference store): 05:242 'discover_rotation (decodes when absent as 0, the value a fresh WatchState starts at; STO-30)' and 05:533 'WatchState.discover_rotation (0)' describe an integer, but the reference store's WatchState.discover_rotation is a Vec<FederationId> (wallet-fedimint/src/journal.rs:301). A wallet written to the set writes 0 where every existing store holds an array and cannot read those stores (OVR-14), and vice versa. That is MISTYPED, not untyped. spec-60q owns the cursor/rotation semantics and lands first; this bead then fixes the bytes. Corrections to the fix: do NOT give every field a STO-30 default — STO-30 governs particular compatibility additions, not all historically required fields; state JSON representation and numeric domain, required vs nullable vs omittable, existing missing-field behaviour, defaults only where compatibility needs them, unknown-field behaviour by citation. Much is inferable and should be CITED, not re-defined: db_prefix u32 (STO-3), occurrence u64 (STO-12), discover_cursor? a FederationId (API-32 renders it), discover_backlog bool (ALC-28), the STO-25 attempts/occurrences from STO-9/DOM-16. Genuinely open: discover_rotation (above), joined_at's integer type, EvacuationSupersessionRecord fields (the reference types them as STO-25 lists, with old_cap_components: Option<EvacFeeCap>). Fold in three unfiled minors of the same class: STO-13:264-265 'every *_msat/_cap/_target/… is Msat' vs its own 'auto_join_lifetime_cap … are u32' two lines later (the explicit u32 field is a count — fix the wording); STO-5:72 'InviteCode (only in CandidateRecord.invite)' needs the sentence that FederationInfo.invite is a plain String not parsed at decode (FMI-20:104-105 relies on it; the reference stores String); OVR-14:112 '(STO-29–STO-31, which own the reference encoding)' vs STO-5:58 'this rule is the single owner of that encoding' — one owner. Include decoding examples for a valid current row, a missing required field and each supported legacy omission.

title: User move / receive / direct-inflow have no default fee_cap, though the resolved value enters the operation key and admission
description:
MAJOR, promoted from the minors by all four. 04-api-contract.md:265-266 (API-19): 'occurrence is required and, with the resolved fee_cap, is part of the operation key' — how fee_cap resolves is not stated; 04:294-297 (API-21): fee_cap? with no resolution rule; 04:576-578 (API-41) points back to 'the daemon-side policy defaults of API-18/API-19/API-21', but only API-18 (pay) states one ('fee_cap defaults to the policy's max_fee'). 01:124-126 (DOM-15): max_fee is 'absolute, for user verbs and probe legs' — the only hint. 03:597 (OPS-29) gives the Move row a base only for the allocator's stamp ('floor(amount × max_fee_bps_of_move / 10 000) stamped by the allocator, ALC-7'); a user move is not allocator-stamped. The default decides the move:<from>:<to>:<amount>:<fee_cap>:<occurrence> key (STO-6) and the money bound the wallet enforces, so two implementations derive different keys and pay different fees for the same request. Fix: API-19 and API-21 state 'fee_cap defaults to Policy.max_fee' (citing DOM-15); split OPS-29's Move row into a user row and an allocator row; API-41 and the CLI grammar (spec-ee9) cite it. One-line major.

## Second review (2026-09-23, four-model bead review round 2: Fable, Opus, Astra, Sol)
CONFIRMED; the fix ratifies what the reference does (every daemon and CLI money verb resolves fee_cap.unwrap_or(policy.max_fee)). More than a one-line major (Astra): OPS-29's Move row has THREE cap sources, not two — (1) user move: explicit cap or the resolved default (Policy.max_fee, DOM-15 'for user verbs'); (2) allocator funding move: the proportional planning cap; (3) probe leg: the persisted session's cap (ALC-27 'amount and leg cap win over the caller's', with the OUT leg's stricter bound). Resolve user defaults ONCE in one owner, API-19/API-21 cite it, API-41 and the CLI grammar refer to the daemon behaviour (standalone verbs resolve the same way). Define when the resolved value becomes immutable for key construction and attachment (it enters the operation key). Scenarios: omitted vs explicit-default request; a policy change between submissions; a probe resume. spec-ee9 lands after this.

title: ALC-29 auto-join counters (lifetime, weekly, concurrent_unproven) and ALC-28's rotation cursor are undefined
description:
MAJOR, promoted from the minors (Opus, Astra, Sol). 06-allocator-and-automation.md:424-428 (ALC-29) gates auto-join on lifetime, weekly and concurrent_unproven without defining their populations (which rows: agent join:<fed>:<nonce> rows? excluding STO-35's re-open note? repaired rows? corrupt records?), the week boundary (rolling vs calendar, inclusivity — the 7-day window is defined only for probes, ALC-26), terminal statuses, or what 'unproven' means (AutoJoined not Passed?); 03:600-611 (OPS-42) supplies only one excluded no-op string; 05:582-594 (STO-22/STO-35) give ledger-scan hints only. 06:403-405 (ALC-28 step 3) takes 'a rotation window of max_candidates_per_pass from the stored cursor and rotation (STO-12)' without the cursor advancement or wrap rule. These decide which federations the agent joins, and 10:198-208 (CNF-17) exercises one successful auto-join, no limit. Fix: ALC-29 defines each count (counted events, durable source rows, time boundary, approval/probe transitions, reopen and failure treatment); ALC-28/STO-12 define exact cursor advancement and wrap; scenarios at, below and above every limit (in the coverage bead). Depends on spec-nwm (how agent-created vs user-created joins are durably identified).

## Second review (2026-09-23, four-model bead review round 2: Fable, Opus, Astra, Sol)
CONFIRMED, PARTIAL on the cursor: ALC-28 step 5 (06:419-422) already says 'advance the cursor over attempted ids only; wrapped iff the window completed, auto-join completed (or stopped for budget) and the plan wrapped; backlog = !wrapped && universe non-empty'. title: A probe session with a no-attempt outcome (preflight failure, umbrella-only failures, key collision) is never cleared: ALC-27 needs a complete outcome table
description:
MAJOR (P1). Rewritten 2026-09-23 after the second four-model bead review; this text replaces the original (which covered only the preflight case and read an omission as a prohibition).

**The defect (verified).** 06-allocator-and-automation.md:361-367 (ALC-27): begin a session (STO-26); write the umbrella `probe:<fed>:<nonce>` row (STO-6); then preflight — "where a failure is a no-attempt that changes no verdict". 05:475-476 (STO-26): the session is "cleared in the same transaction that appends the attempt" — STO-26 defines no no-attempt cleanup transition, so a no-attempt outcome leaves the session and a non-terminal umbrella row. 06:763-766 (ALC-52): "retained sessions first … If any retained session is admitted this cycle only the retained group is admitted and fresh probes are deferred" — one session whose preflight keeps failing starves every fresh probe. 06:352-356 (ALC-26): `active = uncosted non-terminal umbrella rows`, "retained while active || age < 7 d" — the row reserves budget with no age limit. STO-24 never repairs `probe:` rows. The leak is WIDER than preflight: ALC-27 also names "Stranded, Refunded, a Failed leg IN, and an ambiguous record are umbrella-only failures that record no attempt", and DOM-21's probe/user key collision ("the probe records no attempt, as for a preflight failure") — every one of these leaves the session and umbrella row behind. There is also a crash gap between session creation and the umbrella-row write. CNF-16's "records nothing" (10:194-195) is wrong on the same facts; spec-pz6 fixes the assertion, the behaviour is decided here.

**Fix.** ALC-27 owns a complete OUTCOME TABLE for a probe session: retain (an attempt appended, session kept for the next leg), complete-with-attempt, complete-without-attempt (every no-attempt outcome above: preflight failure, umbrella-only failures, the DOM-21 collision), and preempt (OPS-35's "probe preempted by evacuation; no attempt recorded" is the template). For complete-without-attempt: clear the session and terminalize the umbrella row `Failed` with the reason and `cost_msat` (None when no leg moved money; the amount when a leg did), in one transaction, nonce-fenced. No explicit retry bound is needed: once the umbrella row is terminal, ALC-52's `last_invocation` ("the newest max(created_at, updated_at) over agent Probe rows with reason ActiveProbe") already pushes the candidate's `due` to `last_invocation + retry_backoff`, and ALC-26's `active` stops reserving. State the crash gap (a session with no umbrella row is cleared at the next cycle, or the umbrella row is written in the session's own transaction). STO-26, ALC-26, ALC-52 and OPS-35 cite ALC-27.

**Scenario here:** a candidate whose preflight fails twice, restart in between; a fresh probe of another candidate is then admitted, the budget reflects no phantom reservation, and `history` shows two `Failed` umbrella rows with the reason.

Owner: ALC-27. Depends on nothing. spec-pz6 depends on this bead.

title: Tick ledger order: ALC-4 says one tick's rows follow the emission order, ALC-53 writes the advisory refusal rows after the loop
description:
MAJOR, new finding (Astra), verified. 06-allocator-and-automation.md:80-86 (ALC-4): 'The emission order is therefore: for each federation in snapshot order, its Evacuate or evacuation refusal, then the suppression twin …, then its advisory OverCap; then the spending step's decisions; then the standby step's … The ledger seq order of one tick's rows follows this order (ALC-34).' 06:794 (ALC-53): 'The advisory refusal rows are written after the loop'. An early federation's advisory followed by a later federation's evacuation yields opposite seq orders under the two rules; STO-18's counter fence forbids reserving seq holes to reconcile them. Observable on history. Fix: choose the observable row order under ALC-34 (emission order, or decisions-then-advisories) and align ALC-4 and ALC-53 without weakening the atomic intent/ledger admission; CNF-13's assertions follow. Owner ALC-34.

## Second review (2026-09-23, four-model bead review round 2: Fable, Opus, Astra, Sol)
CONFIRMED (P1 by rubric; P2 by impact — nothing reads one tick's internal seq order). The chosen order must also place rows ALC-4's emission order does not mention: deferred-goal refusal rows (ALC-34), conflict-suppressed twins, tick-drop rows, and best-effort rows OVR-4 permits to be absent (do not promise them). Recommend: tick row, then executable decisions and their drops in emission order, then advisory, deferred and suppression rows in emission order (what ALC-53/ALC-36 already say); ALC-34 states it and ALC-4's last sentence becomes a citation. Check ALC-36's standalone tick path. CNF-13 alone does not exercise the conflict: add a fixture with an early advisory refusal and a later executable decision, with enough destination capacity that both are constructible, checked on resident and standalone paths.

title: FMI-42 set-aside duration is 'a constant of the implementation': zero satisfies it and recreates the livelock ADR-0029 exists to stop
description:
MAJOR, promoted from the minors (Opus, Sol; Astra keeps it minor). 02-fedimint-integration.md:202-211 (FMI-42): 'the skip-until duration is a constant of the implementation, not a Policy field'; ADR-0029:120-140 says only 'for a while'. A zero or negligible constant satisfies no stated predicate and the next attempt re-selects the pair that just failed to perform — the livelock ADR-0029 §3 names. It is also a prerequisite for a set-aside scenario (CNF-21 asserts only that a stall does not strand the move). Fix: FMI-42 states a positive minimum (or a bounded backoff), its clock semantics (monotonic, per process), and when the set-aside resets (a successful performance, a restart); extend CNF-21 with a second selection that avoids the pair within the interval. Owner FMI-42.

## Second review (2026-09-23, four-model bead review round 2: Fable, Opus, Astra, Sol)
CONFIRMED (P1 kept; P2 defensible). Say WHO picks the number: name a value or a derivation (recommended: at least the scheduler's min_interval_secs, so the next cycle cannot re-select the pair) — do not leave the agent to invent one. A positive minimum alone does not prove progress (Astra): a positive interval can expire before every next attempt, so the same failing cheapest route can still win forever; state the observable exclusion contract in FMI-42 — when it begins, which subsequent selections honour it, when reconsideration is permitted, restart behaviour (the record 'is not persisted', so a resident host carries it and a standalone invocation carries none — say so; do not prescribe a clock primitive). Scenario here (CNF-21 amendment is THIS bead's, removed from the coverage bead): a failed preferred route and a viable alternative; the next fresh selection takes the alternative; committed-route replay (OPS-20) preserved.

title: DOM-5 'exactly one current ledger row' vs OVR-4 best-effort rows that MAY be absent; ALC-44's stale-plan status failure has no API-15 code
description:

(2) 06:660-663 (ALC-44): 'the resident host's status MUST fail with that error' for a stale replacement plan; 04:203-208 (API-15) 503 list is closed and does not include it; API-6 maps no other 5xx. (b) ALC-44's 'the resident host's status MUST fail with that error' has no API-15 code → add the mapping in API-15 consistent with API-6, preserving the standalone warning/scored view; note the live tension that API-15 503s on 'probing errors (status probe failed: <error>)' while FMI-25 drops an erroring federation and continues — say which wins. title: Conformance coverage (i) security and transport: FMI-40 egress classes, FMI-19 component-wise limits, API-2/SEC-2, SEC-14, API-35, HST-33, FMI-38
description:
MAJOR (P1). Rewritten and SPLIT 2026-09-23 after the second four-model bead review: this bead is now family (i) **security and transport** only; families (ii) the FMI-7 vector, (iii) retry/watchdog/host-failure/fences and (iv) allocator budgets and limits are their own children of spec-yxp (titles begin "Conformance coverage (ii)/(iii)/(iv)"). Where a scenario cannot exercise a requirement (SEC-2's constant-time compare), write the sentence in the requirement that review evidence, not a scenario, demonstrates it.

**Family (i) — requirements chapter 10 cites nowhere (verified by grep at 4ea6c02):**

- FMI-19 component-wise gateway schedule limits (zero citations): a schedule with `base` under the limit and `ppm` over it, on send AND on receive → refused; the pinned SDK (72b1e5be) compares lexicographically, so this is exactly the scenario that catches the reference implementation — it goes in chapter 10 without a result (10:5-7).

title: Retry re-adopts the failed attempt's raw artifacts: OPS-10 / STO-9 never clear operation_id and invoice, and OPS-18 resumes the old operation
description:
MAJOR, Opus, verified (round 2). 05-persistence.md:169-190 (STO-9): the Intent row carries operation_id (raw Pay/Receive artifact) and invoice (raw Receive artifact). 03-operation-lifecycle.md:151-163 (OPS-10): the retry write 'writes Pending at attempt + 1, deletes the cached move record, appends a fresh ledger row and repoints the key index' — it never says the intent's operation_id/invoice are cleared, and STO-9's retry clause ('moves the 0x04 entry from Failed to Pending, deletes the 0x02 move row, appends a fresh ledger row and repoints 0x06') does not either. 03:365-366 (OPS-18) begins: 'If the intent records an operation id: require the intent's invoice (Permanent), run the committed-fee check below and return Awaiting'. So a retried raw Receive re-adopts the failed attempt's operation — against OPS-1 ('a retry can never adopt the operations of the attempt that failed') — and a retried EXPIRED receive re-yields the expired invoice and fails again; a retried raw Pay that recorded an operation id is already refused by OPS-10, so only Receive is live.
Fix: OPS-10 owns the retry write; state that it clears operation_id and invoice (the failed attempt's artifacts stay in its ledger row, STO-15/STO-35, and in the client operation log under the old correlation key, STO-34); STO-9 cites. Decide the interaction with spec-5gn's orphan: a retry of a Failed receive that recorded an operation id either is refused like pay (symmetric) or proceeds with the old contract addressable via spec-cuw's older-attempt addressing — one rule, stated in OPS-10. Scenario: an expired raw receive retried mints a NEW invoice under attempt 1's correlation key; the old operation id is visible only in attempt 0's row. Owners: OPS-10, STO-9. Depends on spec-cuw (same OPS-10 write and the addressing decision).

title: Two fixtures are not constructible as written: CNF-53 admits an automated move into a federation with an empty vetted list; CNF-21 posts a pay from a source held by a probe
description: MAJOR (a scenario that cannot be constructed cannot be judged), Astra, verified (round 2). (1) 10-conformance-checklist.md:100-109 (CNF-53): 'Given the environment except that B's vetted list is empty throughout … when an automated move into B is admitted with no override, then it stays Pending, retryable, with nothing minted'. docs/adr/0030:100-101: 'The allocator never creates a move into a federation whose probe finds no vetted gateway', and ALC-32 plans only over probed, eligible destinations — so no automated move into B can be admitted in that fixture. Fix: use a valid prior admission followed by route loss (the move was admitted while B had a vetted gateway, which is then removed), or distinguish a user-admitted move from the allocator-created case; CNF-53 cites ALC-32, OPS-11, FMI-14. (2) 10:249-258 (CNF-21): 'a scheduled probe held in flight by it [a hanging gateway], when a pay is posted, then its first outbound request reaches a federation or gateway while the probe's connection is still open' — but OPS-6 item 6 (03:90) refuses 'a source federation held by an in-flight probe session → fed_held_by_probe', so a pay whose source is the probed federation is refused at admission and never makes an outbound request. Fix: name a second funded source for the pay (the fixture has A and B; the probe holds one), state the expected immediate refusal for a pay from the held source as a separate assertion, and give the driver-cap clause enough funds/reservations to be constructible. Owners: CNF-53, CNF-21 (the scenarios); no weakening of OPS-6 or ADR-0030. Depends on nothing; spec-7lk amends CNF-21's set-aside clause separately — coordinate.

title: walletd mnemonic / restore-mnemonic under the resident lock: STO-2 says run only while no host holds it, HST-29 names only standalone as refusing and init as blocking — hang or error?
description: MAJOR (P1 by the rubric — Opus, Sol: two compliant hosts diverge observably, a script sees a hang vs an error; Fable, Astra would keep P2). 05-persistence.md:29-30 (STO-2): the one-shot commands 'run only while no resident host holds the lock'; 08-hosts-and-deployment.md:141-143 (HST-29) says refusal is 'for the standalone process alone' and names init as 'the one one-shot command that blocks'. Whether mnemonic / restore-mnemonic block, refuse, or time out while walletd holds the lock is unstated. Fix: one sentence in HST-29 (the owner) naming the behaviour for each one-shot command; STO-2 cites. Scenario: walletd running; mnemonic invoked → the stated behaviour, with the exit status. Depends on nothing.

title: Invites carrying api_secret are 'live credentials' (SEC-24) but SEC-6 has no redaction rule and API-9 / API-17 / list-feds emit them in clear
description: MINOR (P2). 07-security-requirements.md:157-159 (SEC-24): an invite carrying api_secret 'is a live credential and MUST be stored and shared as one'; SEC-6 explicitly protects the seed, the token and the password but supplies no rule for invite secrets in logs or diagnostic errors; the registry row, list-feds, /v1/federations (API-9), API-17 and CandidateView carry the invite in clear under SEC-1 only. Either SEC-24 says the wallet's own copy is protected by SEC-1 and the credential rule binds the operator's handling, or SEC-6 gains a redaction rule for logs and error text (the API is inside the token boundary and may keep the intentional authenticated export surfaces). Decide; do not leave a MUST with no mechanism. Owners: SEC-6 (logging/error boundary), SEC-24 (scope sentence). Depends on nothing.

title: API-16 actor_queue_depth names one design's actor and has no defined meaning (refactor test on a wire field)
description: MAJOR (P1 by the rubric — Astra, Sol: a required wire field two implementations fill differently and a caller cannot use; Fable, Opus would keep P2). 04-api-contract.md (API-16) requires actor_queue_depth on the status/health view with no behavioural definition or domain; a conforming engine need not have an actor queue, and the name fails the refactor test (README: no code structure in requirements). Fix: define an observable quantity ('requests admitted but not yet processed by the admission point') and its value in implementations with no such queue, or make the field nullable and deprecated; align API-39's rendering. Owner: API-16. Depends on nothing.
